content: Be Careful if Using iCloud for Photos. I’ve been using Google photos for years and the app too. Everything was fine until the recent upgrade. Don’t believe Google Photos. There is no reason to have the option to limit access of phone photos and then have the app refuse to work if full access is not granted. This is ridiculous and a round about way of eliminating iCloud. I simply do not want Google Photos having this much control over my iPhone pictures. They are separate for good reason. You MUST give customers the ability to use the limited features on the phone. I don’t see why I cannot use Google Photos App simply to access my photos on Drive. It should be straightforward and VERY easy to give the right access without the all/nothing approach to using the app. Deleting pictures doesn’t work, not backing up STILL backups the phone screenshots and pictures immediately. I have now deleted the Google app waiting to see what to do next, but from the reviews; it seems this is a known problem. Google photos app was fine until you started trying to displace iCloud. Please be transparent as what you’re saying doesn’t match what your app is doing. Better yet - make it do what you say it’s supposed to do. It must be possible to use the standalone app on my iPhone without you accessing my iPhone pictures. I cannot ONLY have access to my Drive pictures only on the computer. I’m writing this review finally because I’m too frustrated the the Google photos app.

title: Way better than iCloud/iPhone Photo storage
content:

title: Very good photo app
content: Very good photo app. This is definitely the best free solution to organizing photos and better than most of the paid ones. It is easy and intuitive to use. It requires very little organizing on the part of the user as the automated organizing is excellent. Moving my photos from my full Dropbox account to this was easy, although it did require an actual computer and not a phone or tablet. There are just a couple of things I don’t like. When you sync from your phone to the app, you can’t select which photos to upload, it’s all or nothing. And if you delete a photo from the app it also deletes it from your phone, in other words you can’t have a photo on your phone and not in the app. Not a big deal really but occasionally there are pics you don’t really need to save, or they are blurry, etc. It does allow you to delete from your phone without deleting from the app, so you can free up space on your phone. And you never have to worry about losing your pictures again!

title: My favorite app since 2011
content: My favorite app since 2011. I absolutely love this app. It’s user friendly, downloadable on any device, has a ton of storage, and is easy to set up because it’s connected to your Google account and settings. It’s such a part of my life that I do t even see it as a hobby, more like a way I experience life. However, I’m very clumsy and loose or break my phone often. There were so many pictures I’d spent hours upset to have lost; all safe and able to be viewed and shared. Nowadays I make sure this is the first app that I download on any device that takes pictures.

Follow the same format you have for the Google Drive app which allows you to organize your files into folders; once the file is in a folder it doesn’t show in your files list. Once you add a photo to an album it shouldn’t show in the photos list, making it easier to keep things organized and manage storage space better. When you have thousands of photos you're trying to organize and you have to scroll through all the photos you already put in an album to get the the photos you haven’t organized yet it’s too much. I also love that I can use this as a FREE photo storage back up from my hard drive. It’s great peace of mind having a virtual hard drive that doesn’t require a monthly fee.

Recommended improvements: 
1. A duplicate photo search function - with our shared library it naturally duplicates a lot of images and it would be a huge time saver if google photos could recognize duplicates for review to delete 
2. A portrait orientation function that flipped sideways photos to the correct view. Having to edit each image can become time consuming. 
3. Ability to modify videos and collages.
4. The Face recognition technology has added to my library the zoomed in images of the people it’s recognizing. Which I had to then go in and delete those images. 
5. This is more for Apple than within google’s control. I use an iPhone and Mac and it would be so nice if when sending images or posting images I could select from my google photos library vs. my phones photo library alone. I have to go and screenshot or save the image from google photos to be able to use. - sidenote, some of the images don’t allow me to save to my photos, which requires me to screenshot them. Not sure why some photos allow me to save and some do not. Could be an Apple issue, but still a nuisance.  

Overall, I have great things to say about this app and recommend it to everyone I can!

title: Google photos
content:
Google photos. I really enjoy being able to set up albums for my photos.  I don’t understand why sometimes I try to delete a duplicated photo and it automatically deletes all of that photo (not just the duplicates).  I’m certain that it’s something that I’m not doing right, but how do I fix this issue?  Are those photos going to archive or the cloud?
The only other thing I’m having a difficult time with is the two Google photos.  Some of my photos are put into a second Google photos section and I’ve had to make albums for these and I can’t understand how to move them to just one set of albums.  Can you make this easier or explain why it does that?  Other than these two issues … I really thoroughly enjoy Google photos.  I am extremely grateful to have memories saved into my albums of photos I’ll treasure until I die (i.e. photos of my some who recently passed away or the great photos of my pregnancy and of my children growing up)!

title: Google photos rocks!!
content: Google photos rocks!!. I used Google + and love that app for sharing photos when I had my Samsung galaxy phones over the years... but then my kids bought me an iPhone and wasn't sure what to do with it as well as wondered if you Google apps would work on it. But it does back up using the assistant and opening the app. I also have iCloud storage and have no idea how to retrieve or see those photos?! I am just trusting my 19,565 photos are there!? But they are on Google Photos thank you thank you very much Google! I don't have a computer but use my husband's to store on an external hard drive. I guess I'm just worried that I will lose this phone and lose all these pictures so I'm grateful for Google photos!I will go figure out how to do the facial recognition piece and look forward to learning as much as I can about this app! It's hard to teach an old dog ... Senior citizen...new tricks... But I am willing to learn!!

title: Its over
content: Its over. The one thing that made Google Photos stand out above having photos just stored on iCloud was the fact that it was free. (Also, Google photos was once unique in organizing photos in cool collections, but google photos is now way behind.) Photos were uploaded in lower quality and were a complete pain to load or download, but it was free and easy to upload photos to. But now that Google wanted to be greedy and is charging increasing amounts for its mediocre photo storage app. I’ve paid the storage subscription for a little while but quickly realized that Apple iCloud costs the same and does a much better job in every aspect. I cancelled the subscription but Google, being petty, made it nearly impossible to download photos back onto device. The app will crash if you attempt to download like 100 items, despite these items all being low quality (because google downgrades the upload quality and ruins the photos/videos permanently.) Please make it easier to download everything so I can finally delete this headache of an app from my phone.

title: Backup automatically turned on
content: Backup automatically turned on. I like the app, but I never set it up to Backup my device and photos, as I use Apple cloud.  Had it for years like that.  It seems like in their last update or somehow, they did something to automatically upload photos from device without any approval.  I hardly even open the app, was only using it to cast my local pictures.   Somehow backup got turned on and then filled the cloud storage, asking me to pay for more, very convenient auto switch.   I think that move was quite wrong and unauthorized, as I didn’t want my photos on their cloud at this point.  I was able to delete them all from cloud, after quite a bit of work, since they also don’t make that part easy, but wanted to make everybody aware of this,  as even deleting those photos from their cloud, we all know they will keep copies somewhere, privacy out the door.  Completely wrong move from their part in my opinion.

title: Love Love Love Google Photos
content: Love Love Love Google Photos. Here I was for the last 3 years struggling with my iPhone trying unsuccessfully and paying to use "The Cloud" to keep my photos! Then while purchasing my new phone I asked about how the cloud worked because I couldn't get my photos on my computer (it's windows not apple) my tech guy says why not use google photos....it's easy. He was right...he downloaded all my photos from my old phone to google photos explained how it worked which if you use google you know it's very user friendly.. I'm so happy now! All those years of paying to struggle with the cloud and now I just use google photo and everything is not only there...it has an assistant that does cool little things like making little videos from my photos.... and the best part it will automatically be on google on my windows computer... now that's an app I can stand behind. Thank you Google Photos!!!

title: Please Improve Video Player/Google Drive constantly fills up storage now.
content:
Please Improve Video Player/Google Drive constantly fills up storage now.. To make it short:
- please improve the video player by adding skip forward and skip back. The timeline is too small.

I’ve updated my score, but I can’t give it a 5 until they improve the Video Player and add a “Double Tap to go back 10 seconds” feature. I also wish there was a way to separate the albums you made yourself from the albums Google helped you make.

Ever since "Google Photos and Google Drive no longer sync", my 17 GB of storage keeps filling up and ruining my flow of things. Apparently this move was made to "stop confusion from customers". Ironically, I've never been this frustrated with Google in my 9 years of using its services.

When I save a video to my PC, i want to see the Backup and Sync take the video to Google Photos, and ONLY google photos. I don't need Google Drive to handle my photos, but it seems like there's no way for my photos to get uploaded to GPhotos without going through GDrive first. No matter how much I read the new instructions and played around, there was no information to tell me how to stop the quota from maxing out everytime i delete a bunch of things to temporarily bring it down.

I would love for Google team to respond to this review with direct instructions before i rate it back to five stars.

Other concerns are that there is no "skip back" button so making it irritating to skip to a specific point in a really long video.

title: The worst App experience ever
content:
The worst App experience ever. I used to send my images between devices using Google Drive. It worked good for a few months until I always had problems about storage. I don’t know why, since my Drive was empty. It said ALL 15GB was used in Google Images, I don’t know why it would send them to this app especially without telling me. I usually delete a lot of images I don’t need anymore, but Google Images works differently. It automatically steals every image and video and saves it as-well, but whenever I delete an image from my device, it still exists in my Google Images. BUT this doesn’t work vice versa, meaning that whenever I delete an image from Google Images, IT ALSO deletes it from my main device. What was the thought process behind this??  
Along with this horrible abomination of an app, it’s terribly unreliable with saving some images. I’ve lost multiple important images at random times, I assume it’s due to low storage. But I can’t do anything about my storage unless I want to delete it from my device altogether, and it doesn’t even ask me before deleting them. 
Lastly, it’s buggy as hell this is awful.

title: I enjoy it but would love to have...
content:
I enjoy it but would love to have.... I would like to see an option added where I can select photos I want to add to photo folder I’ve already created; and be able to search for the folder I want after hitting the plus sign...instead of having to scroll through them all to find the one I want. I have way to many folders to scroll and often miss the one I’m looking for. 

I know I can arrange them alphabetically or by last modified but they are not in either of those orders when your click the plus sign to add photos to a folder. It seems like they get put in order of recently accessed but I don’t always want those ones. A search option for the folder I want after selecting the photos I want to put in said folder would be helpful. Otherwise, I love google photos for due to space and ability to share pictures or whole albums with my family.  I was paying for additional space on apple because I have well over 100k pictures. I love pictures. 

Thanks!

title: Google backups
content: Google backups. I lost 15 years that I can’t ever get back because I trusted google! My account got hacked and google refused to help me get my account back! I offered my ID, police reports, phone bills that showed my email address, everything I could think of! They would rather assist the hacker!!! I lost all my children’s photos, my dads voicemails  (and he’s deceased) not to mention my identity because they hacked all of my financial accounts and ruined my credit. Honestly, I could care less about my credit, I could minimize those losses, I cannot recreate my children’s lives or bring my dad back from the dead!!!  My entire Gdrive (income tax returns, credit card statements, notes, etc.)  all my google photos,  my emails, my contacts, my bank accounts, stock accounts, passwords, maps and map history... EVERYTHING!!!  Then I had my account set to notify a contact and allow them to download everything upon a certain time of inactivity. The day comes when the notice arrives and I am so grateful, but guess what... IMMEDIATELY, the account is accessed to prevent me from obtaining anything!!! BE MINDFUL of what you TRUST google with! You may support them; however, they DO NOT support you!

title: Don’t feel like paying Apple for more data?? Download this app
content:
Don’t feel like paying Apple for more data?? Download this app. Those 1080 and 4K videos and pictures were eating up my storage space on my phone and I didn’t want to pay $4.99 for more space. I had used the app on my previous phone but decided not to bring it forward to my iPhone 12 (insert buzzer sound). After while I was forced to delete unused apps and constantly archive photos. 

I really liked the apps option to store the photos at a lower quality and to archive older photos that aren’t being accessed or don’t contain any valuable content (ie., screenshots of YouTube/TikTok videos). 

My only gripe was the app did take a while to add my 2 years worth of photos. It will perform faster with the app open, but that means I’m unable to mindlessly use my phone for social media purposes. The option to auto-delete my photos after they were uploaded to the Google cloud almost made up for the length of time required to upload photos.

The facial recognition algorithm seems to be a tad better than Apple as Google doesn’t think my “so called” black children all look alike, like Siri does. I do feel it’s almost too good as it has started to auto-add new photos to my previously created photo albums. It did ask for my permission at one point (I think?). One recommendation I would offer is to add the option where Google asks periodically am I apply with the auto-populate options.

Happy space saving!

title: Surprisingly Hesitant With Change
content: Surprisingly Hesitant With Change. I’ve never used Google Photos prior to this week, and now Verizon states I had to if I wanted to have easy access to all my devices photos once I activated my new phone and they weren’t just hanging out there in the, seemingly impossible to enter, iCloud storage. So far it’s been a refreshing change with and super easy to navigate thus far. The only thing I’ve come across as a flaw is, even though it states that the backup is complete and all photos have transferred successfully, sometimes when scrolling through my photos to choose one to view it will be crystal clear but when I click on it to view it solely it becomes extremely blurry. Why???? Besides that I only have 1 more thing that I find as a flaw, one that drives me crazy at that, and that’s the fact on some occasions it can take forever for some of my photos to pop up for viewing status!! I certainly don’t have time for that and in hopes that it fixes itself ASAP on that note!!

title: Amazing so versatile
content: Amazing so versatile. This app is like a personal assistant itself. It can tell you which screenshots and picture are useless at this point so you can go and archive them or delete them. It edits pictures you already have with filters making them so much better, sometimes. If you run out of space on your phone or iCloud well then you can just go ahead put it here on google photos and it will have there ready for you no matter how much space it takes up. After backing it up on google photos you can just delete any photos you don’t want from your phone, and with the assistant feature that does all the editing it can also tell you which photos you can delete because they’re either gibberish, screenshots of something useless, outdated, or they’re practically the same picture as another one, it will tell you. All the picture that are backed up in the app are moved to your google drive so they’ll be same and accessible from any place you can get to google.

title: Great but room for improvement
content:
Great but room for improvement. Enjoy the app but there’s def a few things that would make it so much better...

1.  If I could easily edit automatically generated animations.

Animations in my Opinion are the best part of the assistant feature.  However I hate when it contains one or two photos that I don't like or just aren't a good fit.  For example, it just made one and in half the pictures the person is in sunglasses and half without.  Now I know I could go in and make my own (but really who has the time) but ifi could just go into that animation and adjust it- well that would be so much better!

2. Your location service is pretty off.  Particularly when it puts together a movie it tells me everyone was done in the city I'm from- rather than where the photos were taken.  

3. A little concerned about quality of photos saved.  If I wanted to print them would they be a very high quality still? I've heard the app lowers the resolution.

4. Another animation comment. Annoyed that I couldn't easily edit from the generated animation I decided just once to try and search for those photos and recreate it.  However to select those photos for an animation I had to judge of of the thumb nail and ended up again including one I didn't want. At the very least it would be nice to be able to see the full photos BEFORE turning it into an animation.  But I'd still much prefer to manipulate an auto generated one.

But other than that- I really like it 😊

title: Not at all convenient
content: Not at all convenient. Honestly, google photos is one of their worst apps. It’s a great idea to have your photos in one space with your google account, however the execution of it was not great. First of all, it takes ALL of your storage on your google account. So if you don’t want to pay for extra space, you shouldn’t get it because it takes about 2 seconds for you to run out. Second of all, it is basically required (in order for the app the work) that you sync all of your photos from the device that you downloaded the app. This means that when you try to delete photos off the app (since you ran out of all your space and can’t get any emails) it will automatically delete off your phone which is literally the worst thing. Im saying this to everyone because I lost a lot of my important and meaningful photos since they do not mention this (at least not in a way that was very visible) which ends up sucking for anyone who innocently tries to clear up space. I hope google can make this app more convenient for everyone.

title: A great convinces.
content: A great convinces.. I’m always taking pictures of things. Whether it be family, friends, nature, buildings, or art, I’m always taking photos. These photos would take up all my space and then i wouldn’t have storage for other photos, apps, and etc. I use to be able to transfer them to the computer but when I upgraded our computer wouldn’t take them anymore. I started having to email the photos to myself and then me an Apple associate told me about Google Photos and I live for it. There isn’t a maximum amount that you can put in. You can put in as many as you want.  I have about 1,081 and I’ve had it for about 8 months. I’ve always been satisfied. All you have to do is download the app. Log into your gmail account. It will start to sync your photos. BUT before you go to delete from your camera roll make sure that they are all backed up. You will love it! My Mom and I both live for it and so will you!

title: Hands down
content: Hands down. Has made the most impact on my life compared to any other app I’ve ever used to date. I have had this app for I think close to either 12 or possibly 13 years now and I never imagined how much it would mean to me to be able to look back at my life like that. Constantly surprising myself with photos I forgot existed and randomly brings up memories with loved ones that I’ve lost & I couldn’t be more grateful and thankful to have been able to be reminded of them all no matter how much time has gone by. Probably even more so then before as the years have passed. Don’t hesitate to document your own experiences and history. You’ll regret having not started sooner. Hands down the most important and meaningful app I’ve ever used and consistently so for way longer than any other app I’ve ever downloaded. Thank you for protecting my personal photo journalism.

title: Display in latest update 👎🏻
content:
Display in latest update 👎🏻. Why fix what ain’t broke? Don’t take away the original “day” photo clusters. 

I have enjoyed using Google Photos in the past, with certain updates adding helpful photo editing options (like “portrait” in Suggestions and magic eraser). I appreciate that my photos automatically populate in there and that edits save to my phone. All this is quite useful and intuitive. I don’t understand why they got rid of the daily view of photos, in which photos are grouped by day and then separated by a label and a blank space above the next day’s photo group below. Now everything is in a grid. Google claims that one of them is a “day” view, but all that means is that they’re still chronologically ordered. The tiles are just larger than in “month” view. There is no separation of days or months in any of the three modes. A little date “pill” appears near the top when scrolling, and that’s the only clue users have that they’re looking at photos from a different date. The visual cues are gone. Why take away a format that was working?!

title: Worse and worse
content: Worse and worse. If I could give this app less than 1 star I could. Google Photos genuinely used to be one of the best photo storage and free photo editors available, but with every update they make good features somehow terrible. It's impossible to find anything anymore and the photo editing is split up into so many sections when it used to be neatly organized and accessable. The magic editor was great until they decided to change how to work it for whatever reason and now you have to get all of the thing you want removed in a photo all at once and if you make a mistake you can't just easily undo it, they make you start from the beginning. Even going back to edit previously edited photos will completely erase all the work you've put in before and make you start all over. I hate that they force all this AI editing onto you and make your pictures look even worse than before. I hate this app now and for the first time can say that Apple has a better photo app which is already bad on it's own. Go back to how this app was before the update and everything would be just fine

title: Almost perfect Photos replacement
content:
Almost perfect Photos replacement. Backup is more robust than iCloud sync which gives no control or info on sync progress or settings. Albums are easy to share with permission controls, however adding to shared albums is limited to photos already in Google Photos, and have to manually add pics by date or person (no option to browse by album or memory or any other grouping).

Facial recognition picked up more faces than iOS Photos did, but with less accuracy. No ability to manually add a face when it’s not automatically detected as a face a photo though. 

Import options are limited. Options are sync ENTIRE phone catalog (can’t limit which local albums are synced), import from Facebook or import from iCloud. Would like to specify what I want backed up, and what I don’t. Would also like Dropbox as an import option; also ability for contributors of shared albums to upload new photos from their device.

title: A real treat, GOOGLE PHOTOS, that is!!!!
content:
A real treat, GOOGLE PHOTOS, that is!!!!. Let me be honest, I love mobile phones because it enable me to take photos of anything that catches my eyes. With that said, my pictures would be items, folders or junk archived in some unknown place within my phone or some other storage space, the cloud (one of them….)  Google Photos has turned my thousands of photos into albums, and collages which uplift me spirits as well as those of my love ones.  I am reminded of special all kinds of moments organized in albums which I can retrieve by using easy filters.  For instance by places, by face recognizing of family, friends, coworkers, by dates, by relevancy to a particular event etc.  I may even consider switching careers, movie director and/or producer, my reels (photo grouping  playing functionality) and albums choose the music theme, and suggest titles in case I cant come with my own).
So there,  great job GOOGLE!

title: All around great app!
content:
All around great app!. I've been using Google photos for several years. I can't think of one complaint I'd have about it, so I'll give you some of my favorite features- maybe I'll remember something negative by the time I'm done lol. 

To start, don't turn off personalized suggestions! I love that there's no work involved with it, the app automatically stylizes, makes a collage, creates an album or adds 'color pop' (highlights something/someone & dowses the rest of the pic black & white). Maybe there's more suggestions, but those are what comes to mind at the moment. 

Can you say, 'free unlimited photo storage'?!? That alone is a major plus, having iPhone & not wanting to pay for storage, this helps tremendously! Google goes a step farther & reminds you to clear your clutter- whether that entails deleting the photos from your device or archiving 'junk' photos from the app (screenshots of text & whatnot), the app makes it easy! I love that there even is an archive, more free cloud space for my nonsense! 

Sharing is easy, moreso if you're a Gmail account holder I suppose but easy nonetheless. You can also add Google photos to iMessage apps to make sharing through there just as easy as sending through your iPhone photos. 

Huh, well I guess I was wrong- I can't think of anything I don't like about this app! I could probably go on about what I like but I think this is plenty long enough.

title: Great!
content:
Great!. Fairly long-term user here.. 
never took the time to leave a review, so here goes:
Overall this app is truly a blessing. collages and such are cool but if I’m being picky, they don’t allow many options for preserving the original versions of your files; aside from keeping separate copies of each individual one. Which is fine for creative purposes! I just wish there was an added option to maybe compress albums (like folders on PC or some other file management programs)  i understand-its already a generous amount of (free) storage space offered in the first place. But it’d still be a nice added feature nonetheless. Admittedly, i have horrible file management issues (as in, i hardly do it!) so, in all actuality, I really only have myself to blame for ever running out of space. Just thought I’d share my experience. Regardless, Google Photos is a very solid media backup/storage app and i would definitely recommend it to anyone!

title: Intermediate users and above
content: Intermediate users and above. Hi I’m Ryan and I’m happy that you have a app like this for me I really would love to have everything under one app that I would remember how To use it and have it work for me plus less password signing because now it’s like 5-6 google apps I have to have passwords for all other stuff like everything that it can do is just really awesome and I love it I just don’t like when I get lost and can’t find how to get back to it because I was looking for hours and lost it. Only other thing is I noticed that not all the time does it actually work and n to be having it reset exactly what it was like before I did anything like delete emails by cleaning up my phone space and I’ll ll at the app after about an hour and it’s all back to exactly what It was before deleting pictures and videos and emails each time the next time I even open the app it’s right back to the before I delete anything and stuff.  Sorry but thank you for your kindness to write me.

title: So-far, one word: #FANTASTIC
content: So-far, one word: #FANTASTIC. I had been using the Shoebox app for many many years for trusting them NOT to allow any third-party to have access to my images since it was encrypted (hope you do too #TEAMGOOGLE ). title: Best way to not let photos take up storage
content: Best way to not let photos take up storage. I’ve used google photos for quite a while now and I personally enjoy it. I’m the type of person that likes to record and to take of many things as a safe keeping or memories but that comes with a risk of running out of storage so using google photos is amazing. Every picture and video I take will automatically be put into there and I can clear out my camera roll with being sad or worried about losing at the pictures. It’s like an extra hard drive and it’s free! I also love going to concerts and I usually get so shocked that I forget the concert the night after so I gotta record a lot but it takes up space after so I upload them to google photos and tada I delete them on my camera roll and Im good to go! The only down side to it is that it looks like it bad quality in the apps but if you decide to save it back into your camera roll it’s much better

title: Google doesn’t seem to care about old bugs
content: Google doesn’t seem to care about old bugs. Google tries to make everything automatic and easy.. until it doesn’t. Uploads get stuck, portrait photos seem to particularly struggle. I have photos on my phone right now that google photos refuses to upload. They were there I tried to share them and only half showed to everyone I shared with so I figure I’ll try to reshare. Nope. K I quit app and restart. Nope. K, I’ll sign out sign in and toggle sync. Nope. K, I’ll delete the pictures from the app. Google them forces you to delete them from your phone, but no problem I dig them out of my phones trash and I’ll just reupload and.. back up sync but there not there. K, I’ll repeat all of the above steps. Nope. K, I’ll duplicate the photos in Photos. Hey they there now I’ll just share them.. stuck uploading. K, I’ll just quit the app and.. photos are gone again. K, I’ll just manually add through Photos>select photos I want>square arrow up icon>Google Drive. Yes uploaded. Now to share.. stuck uploading. And photos are gone. There are forum posts a year old on this and google just can’t be bothered to fix it. K, I’ll just use apple’s iCloud.

title: Disappointed about several aspects
content:
Disappointed about several aspects. Disappointed that the date for some photos, particularly old photos that I have scanned and subsequently updated the date using macOS photos, is not brought in as-is. It seems Google is relying on the EXIF dates rather than Apple’s metadata.

Secondly, when I rotate a live photo, it will remove the motion. That’s ok, I thought; I will rotate in Apple Photos which preserves the motion. The problem is that the motion of said photo now appears incorrectly in Google Photos. Apparently when you rotate a Live Photo with Apple Photos, google only sees the image as rotated, not the video. This seems like a bug actually.

The third aspect is that there is no way to scrub. I use the photo “bar” in Apple Photos to scrub quickly between different photos that are very similar. This allows me to detect which photo is the clearest, and to see other subtle differences. With Google Photos I can only swipe between photos. The animation that occurs when swiping causes me to lose context and I am unable to detect those subtle differences. Please add a scrub bar for fast scrolling with no animation like Apple Photos!

title: Impressive.
content: Impressive.. Wow. I’m genuinely surprised that such a massive company could make such a terrible non user friendly app. I was looking to backup my photos from my phone and trusted this app with my camera roll. I accidentally added all of my photos and videos and tried to delete some when I found it deleted from my camera roll too. I did some research to find out how to stop this when I realized I wouldn’t be able to receive any emails because my Google storage was full. I am in between jobs right now so this was a huge stressor and the possibility of my memories being gone from clearing space to get emails really added to it. When I figured out how to stop the app from deleting from my camera roll, I found I couldn’t delete all my pictures from Google photos in a simple manner. I researched the best way to do it and the deleting process took no less than 15 minutes. I had to just hope that my photos and videos wouldn’t be gone from my phone as I took all that time to delete and clear up storage. From what I can tell I don’t think I lost anything but why must it be so difficult.

title: Another baffling fail from Google
content: Another baffling fail from Google. Another once-beloved and once relied-upon Google app being deleted from my phone after over a decade of use. It’s mind blowing, Google is going to be the first company in history to fail due to zero external factors or causes, just their own deliberate choices to absolutely cannibalize their own products. I just cannot understand why they would see people loving and relying on a product and think “let’s destroy every core aspect of this and make it into something that virtually everyone with a pulse absolutely despises”. It was one of the last apps that I still had some safety and security from the vile disgusting AI garbage slop, until today. They removed the “switch to classic search” option that was my last saving grace. I absolutely will not under any circumstances be engaging with their foul nauseating “Gemini” AI moronic waste of 1s and 0s. You really start to wonder if the people who work at this company are embarrassed for it to be known/embarrassed to associate themselves with such a bizarre downfall of a one-time innovative industry leader. Whole thing is sad and just reeks of greed, ignorance, and incompetence.

title: Garbage
content: Garbage. As one other reviewer said, this app lacks the necessary flexibility to be at all useful. I have thousands of photos on my devices. I do not want or need every last one of them backed up in this app but it doesn’t give one the option to pick and choose. And where is it putting them? Who has access to them? Unknown. Also beware this app will take the place of your in-device photo albums— a photo deleted in the app is actually deleted from your device, not just within the app itself. This may be something that can be configured in settings but it isn’t at all clear when navigating the app initially. For something that is supposed to be for storage and organizing photos, I do not like how it so easily manipulates the photos in their original location on my device without asking me. So now a bunch of my photos that I would have preferred to keep only on this device are uploaded somewhere in the ether— can’t delete them in the app without actually deleting them from my device too. This is garbage. I’ve deleted it and will not be re-installing, and hopefully my photos are sequestered wherever they have ended up.

title: Love/Hate & Hot/Cold
content:
Love/Hate & Hot/Cold. App is great with backing up photos, it creates animated-shorts, videos, and mini-movies I probably couldn't have or would have not taken the time to make myself (a LOT of pix of my daughter!! 😍). But It takes too long to backup photos, it feels as though I need to fool around in the app to babysit and ensure everything is uploaded. And though my pix are already in the app, it seems to take EVEN LONGER to gather a few pix and put them in an album! It shows an "uploading" bar forever, and my phone usually hibernates after 1 minute, and when I go back in the album NEVER GOT CREATED! UGH!! 

I had to finally create just my album cover with just one photo, grab a few at a time and babysit those while still in the app to ensure the album was created properly. Not sure if it's an Apple vs Google issue, but you guys need to get it together. The concept of the app is great, but the execution of its functionality is TERRIBLE!! 👎🏿👎🏿👎🏿

title: SO GREAT!
content: SO GREAT!. Aside from just the search engine, Google is a big part of my everyday/digital life; I use it for most everything. My family has Fiber internet and cable, I use Docs for school...the list goes on. And the Photos app is just another one of the things they’ve done right. The automatic backup is great, although at first I was hesitant to enable it because I thought it would take too long to get to all of my photos (however I was proven wrong—it works like a charm as long as you have high internet speeds). Not only does it do the main things you need it to do, but more! It has helpful features such as being able to make albums, the way it automatically identifies certain people/pets, and one of the coolest: Assistant. The assistant tab is so fun because it takes groups of pictures and videos and makes gifs, short movies compilations, and more. I could honestly go on and on. Everything is so great about this app!

title: Awesome and a LIFEsaver!!
content: Awesome and a LIFEsaver!!. Not only does this app work great and creates super cute collages, animations, and mini-movies all by itself (which you can save or delete), but it is the ONLY solution I found to the fact that iCloud/iTunes simply stopped uploading my photos/videos from my iPod 5 (or wouldn’t let me access or download them to my PC), and no other cloud service I tried (like MS’s OneDrive) could “see” that I had over 5,000 items to upload—except Google Photos!!! It was relatively fast and absolutely painless to upload every single one of them to Google Photos, however. (I did happen to upgrade my device to an iPhone 8, which is how I found out the app, so I never tried it from the iPod, but it would likely work, though might have been slower.) In any case, I wanted to post this in case anyone else is desperately looking for the same solution—and to thank Google for providing it, and making a really fun app, too!

title: Tremendous help to photographers
content:
Tremendous help to photographers. I finally solved my photographic workflow process with Google photos. I have a huge library of raw images and finding a person, place or thing to retouch was a super hard problem to solve. I have over twenty years of images. Google photos to the rescue. I shoot in raw + jpeg and upload all the jpegs to google photos, keeping the original file name. My images are also archived offline. 

Then I am able to harness the intelligence of google to identify people, places, and animals. I can search on multiple criteria (such as color, location, etc) and quickly find shots. When I find the image in Google photos I can see the file name and then  can easily locate the correlating raw image in my offline archives to enable high resolution retouching. 

In addition, I carry virtually every shoot I have done on my pocket (on my phone). It is amazing! Thank you Google!

title: Duplicates are a pain; otherwise ✅
content:
Duplicates are a pain; otherwise ✅. Overall I love the Google Photo app. It’s made sharing pictures, both old and new, with my whole family so much easier. 
My biggest complaint is that there’s no easy way to remove duplicate photos that are automatically sent from my iPhone Photo app to the Google Photo app. Currently the user has to go through their entire library manually to find & delete duplicate items. 
There’s also some things I don’t want transferred to the Google app, but users are not given a chance to choose which photos are transferred to the Google Photo app; it’s done automatically. 
Two changes/corrections I would love to see include:

1. Some kind of program written into the app that would pull up all of the duplicate items in my account so I could have the option to delete them w/o having to go thru 3000+ photos manually to remove unwanted copies. 

2. An option to manually select the items in the iPhone Photo app that you want moved into your Google Photo app. OR at least give us a simple auto or manual option until something more detailed can be written.

I’m pretty sure if Google we’re to do a survey on those two items you’d find there’s a lot more subscribers than just myself who would like these ideas. I hope you actually see this feedback and find it helpful.

title: I’ve lost all of the progress on my wedding album twice… and several hours in the process
content: I’ve lost all of the progress on my wedding album twice… and several hours in the process. I tried to put together a wedding album for purchase using my iPhone and Google Photos this afternoon. After working for about an hour (and there is no way to save) The app crash losing all of my progress. Fine it happens. Then I tried to do the same thing using my tablet. I spent about two hours on at this time and was doing less touchups, hit the back button to go out of a page, and the back button freaked out and took me out of the entire album. Again there was no way whatsoever to save so I lost about three hours of my life and I feel like I am about to throw my tablet across the room. This is the most frustrating photo software I have ever used for this sole reason. It’s not that bad otherwise, but I don’t think that I will use Google again and I certainly don’t think that they will get the huge chunk of money that they were about to get for my wedding album. Additionally I will be trying to dissuade everybody I know from using Google photos for this purpose. Please add a freaking save option.

title: I love Google photos
content:
I love Google photos. I’ve been a paying customer for years and tell others to use it. Only suggestion that comes to mind:

My family went on a trip recently. I created a shared photo album and we all added to it from our Google photos. The problem is that my own facial recognition definitions don’t work with their shared photos. I feel like they should still. There are like 1,300 photos and I want to be able to search them all for the few with all our family members included. When I do this, it only returns a couple that I took. I looked at my family’s shared photos for facial recognition but none of them show anything. Maybe this is a legal thing where you’re not allowed to but it just doesn’t make sense to me if they’ve already shared the photos with me and they are running through my facial recognition instead of theirs

title: Impressive with room to grow
content:
Impressive with room to grow. Can’t really say enough great things abt. this app. It literally does everything I could ever think of wanting it do! (and new features are STILL being added all the  time!) 
I probably sound like I’m a google employee... But I (pinky) promise, that I’m not! ..I’m .just another very thoroughly satisfied user of google photos. 
That being said, If I had to choose one annoyance... it would be with the facial recognition features. It does a great job with recognizing people in photos and then creating an album of that person. Included in the album, were videos of ‘recognized’ individuals. I question why there arent settings options for this feature though.... I also wish we could ‘train it’ to recognize more people by creating “People” folders manually. I also wish it was a little more ‘consistent’ with recognizing individuals (especially individuals that had been previously recognized) that appear in mUltiple VIDEOS as well as photos.

title: Warning FREE  UP SPACE freezes
content: Warning FREE  UP SPACE freezes. I am disappointed because the google photo app didn’t work as expected.  I chose google over icloud to backup all my pics and lost about 3k pics from Oct 2019 to today because the google Photos app kept freezing when about 3k photos were updated. I tried multiple times with no success so I deleted the pics from my phone directly since I already saw them uploaded in the photos app, I was just told by my rep that because of the sync function, my photos were deleted from the google photos app too. The free up space was not working. It worked to delete 50 or 200 or 150 pics at a time but froze to delete 3k+ pics. There must be a warning for people to avoid loosing their pics due to sync vs free up space not working and customers should be warned Not to Delete any pics from your phone as free up would freeze when trying to free up over 3k pics at a time. Bad combination. “Warning: Do not delete photos directly from your phone while sync is active even if you see the pics are in the photo app” because of the sync option, your pics will be deleted from the google photo app too. WARNING.

title: I RECOMMEND THIS APP
content: I RECOMMEND THIS APP. READ THIS COMMENT BEFORE YOU GET THIS APP. I’ve had this app for a few years like one or two now. I really like using this app since I am a photographer. The best part of the app is that it takes editing photos to a whole new level. I have a iPhone don’t get me wrong there’s nothing really wrong with how you can edit photos on a regular camera for iPhones but when you use this app it makes the whole photo better like when you put you picture in portrait mode and when you go into the app to edit the photo you have choices to enhance the photo and make the background black and white but the object itself in color and you can make the background even more blurry and since am a photographer everybody always asks me how I make my photos so blurry and how I make the photos that I take nicer than the original well that is how I do it

title: Super Annoying Bugs
content: Super Annoying Bugs. First of all, I’m rating this one star because hopefully that will let it be seen. I really like google photos, heard about it from some family members and they love it. I just downloaded it, but when it uploaded my photos, I synced favorites thinking that it would put my favorites from my photos into google photos. WRONG. Instead, it favorited all of my photos, and now I have to search through all of my photos to find the old favorites again. Secondly, I have to keep readding photos into albums, because I will add them all to a google photos album and then they all are removed from the album for no reason (this has happened to all the albums I made just an hour ago). All in all, I really like google photos and how it has free storage and creates little memories for you, so please fix these bugs so I can enjoy it all the way!

title: One of the best apps in the App Store
content: One of the best apps in the App Store. When I went to Apple and they told me that I was going to completely lose all of my pictures and videos because of a "complete swipe" they had to do on my phone, I thought I was seriously screwed. Since I have a 2 year old, you know my phone is filled with tons of pics and videos. Once I downloaded this app with my existing Gmail email address, I was able to save every single picture and video with this app, and it only took about 30 minutes to backup around 800 images/videos. I also love that it automatically downloads all of my photos from my phone's photo album without me having to manually press a button for my pics to sync.. It's amazing, and I'm so glad I found it. Best part about it - it's free... and I believe I have unlimited storage for all of my pictures and videos that need to be backed up from my phone or my computer. Thanks Google! 😊

title: True As Advertised
content: True As Advertised. I D/L this app for the sole purpose of minimizing my I-Phones overall speed & quality due to the *Apple Photos* app always being the #1, largest size of GB that becomes used & therefore drastically reduces my phones overall speed & function. However, since I have transferred of my photos through the Google photos application I have freed up nearly 1/2 of my current phone plans monthly data allowance/eligibility. I love this app for many reasons and other than allowing for an improved function, The app offers so many different and cool ideas which I've already took an advantage of :D... *On a side note, if you are downloading this app because your storage space is becoming too full you must delete all of your photos and videos through your Apple Photos Account, but I don't feel as if you're going to delete them forever! As that was my biggest fear, but it definitely is a must-have app.

title: Love it.
content: Love it.. Absolutely great app, organizes photos to YOUR preferences, not the phone or devices manufacturer. Tons of free storage with lost cost option to increase it substantially. Non intrusive, non invasive and puts you in control. Easy to use with lots of options on how you can organize your photos AND videos. Secure and stable with the power of Google backing it up. After about 300 pics my iPhone was constantly bugging me my storage was about full and kept pestering me to purchase additional storage from them, now that issue is a thing of the past, I backed everything up to the Google app and deleted everything from my phone, as stated there’s no issues with the app whatsoever, everything is as it should be and just as I left it from the previous access. I’m sold, it’s great. It even has basic photo editing. No issues or regrets whatsoever.

title: Great free photo storage
content: Great free photo storage. If you’re one of those people always running out of memory space on your phone, or are tired of iCloud telling you to pay for more storage space and back up your photos then this is for you. I love the way it saves space on my phone yet has all my photos from the last six years only a touch away. I can access it from anywhere I can email, so transferring pictures between devices or family members is no big deal. The bonus to the free storage and easy accessibility is the random cute features they have. While some are cute, like the movies they compile for you with clips of your kids growing up, some are not very well designed. The photo book option is very basic and lame and the collages are very limited in design. However I don’t fault them for that- I use this as a storage and photo sharing space and in that regard I recommend for everyone! No brainer!

title: Love Google Drive, Chrome, Gmail and definitely love photos so very much!
content:
Love Google Drive, Chrome, Gmail and definitely love photos so very much!. This is such a user friendly app and I feel comfortable and safe with it. The only non-user friendly thing is the folders.  I wish it was as quick and easy to create and sort photos I to files as it is in iOS. I just can’t click and create a folder. It seems it is always taking off somewhere and trying to share or making it difficult to add pics simply. It’s a bit of a run around clearly, as I still have trouble. That is why I keep my Apple photos app, to separate photos, but that is only reason. Google is great in every other way. 
Actually. There is one thing I wish they would just go ahead and add since I’m sure it’s not that difficult. I k ow they have to hold back some things for money, anticipation or whatever the reason, but please, please add a duplicate finder and eraser!   That would make it a five star holy grail for me!!!

title: Beyond Expectations
content:
Beyond Expectations. I got this because I was tired of my phone storage being full. The subscription plans are reasonable if you need the higher amount of memory capacities. Overall, a fantastic find. It creates memories and collages to look back on. It’s intuitive enough to review possible pictures that need to rotate as well as well as help review duplicates. It also will help delete photos that it uploads so you don’t need to worry about accidentally erasing pictures that are unsuccessful in uploading.

The few areas I’d say could use improvement is facial detection (sometimes when you label a person, it’s very good about grabbing those people; other times, it thinks two different people are the same person and the only way to unlink them from being identified/grouped as one person is to tediously go through each picture to identify they’re different. 

I also think screenshots and memes needs improvement since it does not detect many (or splits them up in odd ways).

And last but certainly not least, I hope there’s a way to upload pictures manually. Some of my pictures (especially older ones) have just never uploaded successfully. It simply finishes the backup but always misses these. As such, I’m stuck with about 500-1,000 pictures that are stuck to my phone and unable to upload into my cloud photos storage for whichever reason (I have not discovered the why yet but if I do, will update this review).

Overall though, super pleased with this app. My only regret is not having listened sooner when it was first suggested to me lol because it’s superb and I look forward to seeing how it continues to develop.

title: Well below Google’s standards
content: Well below Google’s standards. Google Drive is a wonderful product, proving the missing features in Google Photos is intentional.  Uploaded about 100 images as a test from my iPad.  Attempted to delete them...but Photos does not allow users to remove photos in bulk.  You must select each and every photo you want to delete.  This reeks of “we have your data and won’t let go.”  Took 700 photos on holiday?  Good luck managing that later. App also does seem to allow any means of direct album organization.  Organize by date automatically only.  Did 4 or 5 very different things that day? Nope, all one album.  You also may not select what photos sync and which do not (again, basic Google Drive functionality) so if you download images or graphics those are mixed in with your photos.  Want to remove a photo from the cloud that doesn’t belong with your photos?  Google will penalize you for daring by deleting it from your device automatically.  This “you will use the product in only the very, very narrow use-case we want you to” is what we expect of Apple, not Google.  Without user flexibility, not at all worth it, even for free.

title: Saves me so much time and space- favorite app.
content:
Saves me so much time and space- favorite app.. Google photos is my favorite app by far. I have photos on here that have been automatically downloaded to the app since 2012. It’s great because once they are downloaded to the app from my phone (which takes seconds) I can delete them off of my phone and save space! Google photos makes it so easy to look for pictures of my friends and it separated them by face and name- even my pets are separated. It also makes it easy to share them and text them to people on any format. Not to mention that it makes random movies and cool animation of photos you take which you can decide to keep or discard. It shows all the places that I’ve taken pictures around the world- there are so many features. 
Google photos is by far the best app on my phone. 
I’ve turned just about all of my friends and family on to the app and they all love it too!

title: Okay
content: Okay. Google Photos stopped hosting unlimited storage June 2021 - I understand, storage isn’t free. But now that this is a paid service, my expectations are higher for a photo management service. I know Google Photos can detect similar photos, but it does not offer a function to clean up one’s similar photos in order to save data. Also, there’s no function to disable uploading videos, which obviously takes up the majority of storage space. Often Google Photos will choke on long 4k videos, wasting time and upload bandwidth only for me to have to delete it anyways because it takes up too much space. Google harvested tons of image data from users to build their algorithms and now that they’ve done that the service has basically stagnated since then and I’ve little confidence in Google adding any features ever again. In fact if it were not for paying for storage I’d just assume Google Photos would be discontinued like tons of other Google services.

title: The of essential apps to have on your phone.
content: The of essential apps to have on your phone.. This app is one of the greatest apps on phone especially if your looking at a smartphone that cost way too much for that high memory space you want. You can literally download this app and have every photo and video you ever owned on this app since it lives in the cloud. Before you even go crazy about the cloud not being secured, google has top notch security to ensure your photos and videos are safe. I’ve had google photo for the past 10 years and I can tell you from experience it has let me down. The backups are fast and simple as long as you have connection. Finding, sharing, organizing photos and videos are simple and easy. You just need a google account or gmail to get started. I love this app and will continue to always use this app. It truly is a great app. Oh did I mention you can access this app on everything? Well done google!

title: If you don’t have this app, what are you doing?
content:
If you don’t have this app, what are you doing?. I am just so thankful that this app exists!
How are they able to give us so much space? I take an obscene amount of photos and it’s truly a lifesaver. It’s easy to use and I like that it gives suggestions on how to clear the clutter and edit. The photo of the day feature is great for recalling fond memories...and for deleting those I’d rather forget. Its face recognition feature is really precise, which would be worrying if it weren’t so awesome. You can also do a keyword search and the results are pretty accurate. Album sharing/having collaborative albums is also great. I’ve yet to use the photo album ordering feature, but I’m glad it’s an option. 
The only thing is that I do wish they would switch back to the old layout, where the Assistant tab (instead of all my photos) is the homepage. It made more sense that way.
Overall, a must have app!

title: The best photo storage app
content: The best photo storage app. Google photos is the best and highest quality photo storage and photo organizer on the App Store. It automatically backs up your photos and stores them safely. I really love this app so much, thanks google for creating this, I also love This because you won’t need to worry about photo storage ever again because they’re safely stored in google photos. I have not had one backup problem and the app works as it should and flawlessly. I have backed up my photos and deleted all of them from apple photos and they’re still in google photos!!!!! 😁. No bugs, smooth experience, great search feature, a good set of features, and simple. The only thing I’d change is to make an in-app camera 📷. Otherwise this app is phenomenal and perfect. Thanks again google, forget apple photos with the icloud message “no more iCloud storage” because this app exists. Sorry cuz this review was a bit long.

title: Great app, missing a couple simple features
content: Great app, missing a couple simple features. Has many options I really like, face recognition, ability to automatically add new photos to albums, great tools to make collages, photo books & movies, easy to share with others and collaborate. It’s lacking in some of the more simple options like the ability to order my albums the way I’d like, be able to sort alphabetically, or by date. I have multiple albums and I spend too much time scrolling through my albums when manually adding photos, and you can’t make an album within an album which would be another simple feature. For Example to make an album titled Christmas, and then be able to have separate albums within, for each year and there isn’t. It’s simply like making sub-folders within a folder like you can do with files and documents. The inability to do simple sorting & filing of my pictures is frustrating because I like so many other features in the app.

title: It’s my favorite photo app, but...
content:
It’s my favorite photo app, but.... I literally have EVERY SINGLE photo of mine sorted into an album. It makes things so easy to find and it’s wonderful. However, I have one major complaint: I can’t delete a photo from the album.
The only option I have is to “remove from album.”
So for example, maybe I have pictures that I took of my food over the years and I have a folder titled “food.” Well I can’t just delete all those useless food pics from the album page. Instead I have to scroll through THOUSANDS of photos in the photo page, hoping to come across my food pics. Or I have to click on the info button, figure out the date I took the picture, try to find that date and delete there from the photos page, and then repeat that for the hundreds of photos that are in that album. 
And that is one of example of the many ways this has inconvenienced me. So PLEASE I’m begging you, just add a “delete” option from the album menu. Please.

title: Love it
content: Love it. Works great and really does a lot of awesome things! I love all the extra features and tools such as magic eraser, and the face recognition, and photo editing features. I am a huge google fanatic. I think they really are one of the best tech companies out there. Google lense is one of the coolest things I’ve ever used with the reverse image search and whatnot. Also they offer a lot of really great services and products at a very good price compared to some other competitors. I’m a Google One member and I like that I can use all their features like VPN or extra backup storage and Google Photos even on an iPhone and all my other devices. They work great everywhere and my Google assistant is very smart…. lol probably much smarter than me. It never fails to impress me what they can do. I trust them with my life when it comes to all things future and technology. Huge fan here

title: Great features!..
content: Great features!... I think this is an xclnt app...I think the way y'all have fine the designs & layouts for pictures its wonderful...grouping them together in colleges I think there should be more features & tabs...
