title: Forcing Full Access is Invasive
content:
Forcing Full Access is Invasive. I used to use this app a lot for photo sharing, but I do not want to give FULL access to my ENTIRE photo library. 

One time, I allowed full access just to test it, and it immediately started pushing me to “back up” all my photos. Including NUDE PHOTOS onto my work email.

After all my personal photos got pushed to Google Workplace Cloud, I started getting charged for storage! I don’t want or need FULL STORAGE, I just wanted to share a few photos. 

Worse, when I tried to delete those nude photos later, I couldn’t find a straightforward way to remove them. I still have over 18k photos sitting in Google Cloud. Why? The newly added photos blended by date across all other thousands photos, so there was no way to Select All recent additions and delete them. 

Now, if I only give LIMITED access to my photo library, the app won’t allow me to upload any photos whatsoever. 

That feels suspicious and monopolistic! No other photo apps I use (IG, FB, editing apps) demand full access like this.

Google knows most people have a Gmail account, and they’re using that convenience to funnel users into giving up privacy to train their AI models on everyone’s photos, while charging them for storage.

When I try using the web browser version, the Google devs have “bricked” / closed up any possible way to share photos without giving them full access to my entire life. 

This is aggressive and privacy-unfriendly. It makes me dislike Google.

title: Privacy Highjacking
content: Privacy Highjacking. Does not allow limited or “no access“ settings to the photos in the camera roll. Can’t use the app for viewing existing or shared albums unless granting full access. Completely pointless and useless app if you don’t want Google to have full access to every private photo. When you switch to the app drawer view or restore the app back to the foreground, you can see portions of the app for a split second. Then Google hides everything under a black screen saying you have to allow full access. It is quite clear they are purposely preventing use of the app until you give them full access. Unacceptable predatory practices. Google Photos should be band from the App Store unless they change it. I feel bad for people that don’t understand how companies like Google take advantage of them and rob them of their privacy… And how they impose or threaten limitations that don’t need to be there so they can convince people to give up their personal data…. So Google can use all that data for their internal purposes. Sad!

title: Love everything except too many notifications
content:
Love everything except too many notifications. I love the Google Photo App: especially the memory collages, surprising special effect photos every now and then, finding similar pictures from the past and making a collage of them, and so on. I just find the notification alerts on the app VERY annoying when you open the app and there’s nothing to be notified of. Sometimes it’s trying to entice you to buy something, like ordering photos, albums, products, but sometimes there’s nothing, as if they just want your attention or want you to just open the app for no apparent reason. We already have a lot of other apps with notifications, we don’t need more distraction. Other than that, I LOVE the app. 😊
P.S. Trying to post this review; I was asked to type in a nickname. Any name I put there, is already taken. This is frustrating and discouraging!😡

title: So many working features
content: So many working features. Really great app with tons of capability, including that the app automatically loaded the following for this review: “Automatically syncs my photos on a day to day basis, archives the uninteresting, stylizes the interesting, makes albums and collages by itself.... and a lot more” ... my biggest issue, though, is the feature that “curates” the pictures that it thinks I want to see on a slideshow. Most of the time they are good pictures, but every few months I scroll through and notice a great or memorable photo that I haven’t seen in a loooong time, that the slideshow just doesn’t serve up because it’s not in the curated list. It would be nice if there was at least a little more serendipity factor. Not for screenshots and whatnot, that’s understandable. But then it completely leaves photos that we took for a reason off the list for the family slideshow. This is meant to be constructive feedback.

title: Great, but improvements needed
content: Great, but improvements needed. I like this app a lot, I got it because I am a car enthusiast that collects in this case emblems/scripts/badges, and this app claims it can identify it. Editing this review, it has greatly improved at identifying cars, and parts. However, when I search a car, ex., 1968 Mercury Cougar, 1967 Chevy Camaro SS, 2017 Dodge/SRT8 Challenger 392 HEMI, when I search these, it used to tell me the year. Now it just brings up the newest things. 1997 Mercury Cougar, 2018 camaro, 2019 challenger, which is the most useless thing I've seen in quite a while. I got this app to identify stuff. Not to bring up ads of something essentially not at all what I want to see. That's BS. I want this thing fixed. The reason I can't delete it is because of free, so far unlimited storage. That's very helpful to me. But the ads - it isn't very helpful, however it isn't completely useless to parts, etc.

title: Love this app but needs a setting change or two
content: Love this app but needs a setting change or two. I love this app and have used it since I was 16. However, sometimes it will back up and upload the same photos several times and that is an enormous pain because you have to manually go through and delete them. I have looked for a setting to remove duplicates or only save originals and I can’t find one. I feel like that should be added to the next update because it would be extremely useful and a time saver. It needs this setting because I can spend hours trying to remove photos to reduce my storage and it takes hours. I can delete over 100 photos and not make a dent in my storage. And it’s my photos taking up my google storage. Please please please add this setting in your next update.

title: Picasa was better for editing and movie making but Google Photos is good job with facial recognition
content: Picasa was better for editing and movie making but Google Photos is good job with facial recognition. I miss Picasa, but Google bought it and pulled the plug. Not nearly as many editing options in Google Photos. Uploading photos from my computer into GP is a real pain. If I have 50 photos to upload into GP from my hard drive it may take 20 attempts before they all upload. And they are saved by upload date, not by photo date. Bring back Picasa! PS. One thing I like about Google Photos is its capability of finding photos by subject, location or category. I wish I could manually add names of people in photos who don’t get picked up by the facial recognition software, such as silhouettes and photos from behind. I wish I can add text to photos to help me remember the locations and subjects, and to be creative with birthday and other celebration social media postings.

title: Just okay, was way better
content:
Just okay, was way better. I’ve had google photos for forever, use to be completely free. Was great to have! Eventually they started charging. So I payed for it. I needed to upgrade unfortunately ran out of storage and had an issue with accidentally paying for two separate accounts and immediately messaged them, took a while for a reason and they wouldn’t give me my money back on the account I never used even though I’ve actually had been paying for one account since they first started charging money for storage. I felt wronged for sure. 
Maybe due to the amount of photos and videos I have but it glitches a lot. I even spent a couple days deleting emails, documents, pictures and videos and it did not change the amount of storage I had available which is impossible so that was very frustrating, I feel I’m being conned into constantly upgrading and paying more.

title: The BIG scam
content:
The BIG scam. Google photos was advertised and offered as free and unlimited photos. Wanting to believe that google would surely standby and support what they had offered and to save space on my phone and in the “cloud”, I let photos be “cleaned out” as they were loaded to my google photos account.  Several years later it’s almost impossible to add those photos back to my phone and I have no idea if they have uploaded onto the cloud since I have turned it on again. However I’m now paying to use the service, if I understood things correctly.  
I have tried to go through and re-save photos of my family, friends and pets especially after both of my parents passed away about a week apart.  Unfortunately doing that re-adds them to google also and trying to delete anything from google photos, deletes the photo entirely.  This is so frustrating.  I’d love to just delete the app completely.

title: Uses waaaay too much data!
content:
Uses waaaay too much data!. I love the app. I think it organizes everything very well, and I appreciate the suggestions and edits it does with some of the photos. However, if you are not connected to WIFI, beware! This app will kill your data. My phone service charged me 3 overage charges in 1 month and I couldn't figure out why because I don't really watch a lot of videos or stream music. It was because of this app running in the background and even more so when I would open it up. 

Only use this app with WIFI! Also, make sure cellular data is turned off for it in your settings, or beware.        

UPDATE: I am so upset that they removed the suggestion section where they would pick some of my photos and suggest different edits or collages with them. That was my favorite feature about this app and now it is gone! Went from a 3 star rate down to 2 because of this removal! Please bring that feature back and I will rate a high 5 stars then for you. Thank you.

title: Albums
content:
Albums. I have now tried two times to create an album and google will not sync the photos. I created one album another time and didn’t have a problem, but this one has been a doozy. Tried to add photos to it last night, had 200 in the album, but it wasn’t showing up on my computer. When I went to check it on my phone again, it had completely cleared out the album. So I added 195 to it today (still don’t know which photos I’m missing) and it won’t show up on my laptop or on another app. I’m frustrated. It shouldn’t be that hard to take photos already on the app and put them in an album! 
I also can’t figure out how to delete multiple photos at once. It always just asks me if I want to move it to the archive. And I can’t add photos from the roll to an album, I have to go to the album and click add photos. There are also over 200 photos still on my phone’s camera roll because they won’t sync to google photos for some reason. Overall, not a great experience.

title: Very very good, but not yet great
content:
Very very good, but not yet great. I love Google, so I may be a bit biased.  Google photos is a really good photo storage and photo sharing app.  I love that they offer unlimited storage, although it is at a decreased quality.  While original quality photo storage is available for a fee, it sure would be nice if Google made it free.  

I love the ability to upload a bunch of photos at once, but often some of the photos are skipped (unclear why).  I like that Google gives notice of the skipped photos, but often when it does this one loses the ability to automatically upload the ones that weren't skipped into an album.  After that, adding photos into an album isn't as easy as it could be.  How about a quick drag and drop feature?

I also love that Google automatically takes certain pictures and creates a computer generated copy with a special filter, frame, or makes a panorama of several photos, giving the Google Photo owner the option of keeping or discarding it.  

The photo search option is also really cool.  I can search thousands of my photos for pictures with dogs, or of Aunt Sue in the snow it Tibet.  It somehow does a really good job of finding these pictures.  It does make some mistakes, like adding wolfs to photos of dogs, but hey, aren't dogs descended from wolfs?  Overall the search, while not perfect, it is really good. 

Overall I would highly recommend Google Photos. Upload your photos from your phone, and if you lose or break your phone, your pictures will still be safe.  I would also recommend uploading the pictures from your computer for the same reason.  Then you can also access them from anywhere through the Google Photo app.

title: Great app, but Problems have arisen
content: Great app, but Problems have arisen. I’ve used this app pretty much since the day it was released, and I recommended it to all my friends, but since an update in the past few months it’s starting to infuriate me. I’ve been a heavy Google+ user for a long time, and I post Car Polls every day using pictures from the web. Well, any picture that I upload to G+ now enters my Google Photos library. I DO NOT want that! To combat this issue, I made a folder for pictures from all my different devices. But that seems to have been a temporary solution. Because now when I try to move items to a folder, and this happens every time — it either takes 4+ hours (not exaggerating) 4 HOURS! Or it doesn’t work at all. So either fix the folder issue or please don’t integrate G+ photos with Google Photos. I don’t want web stock photos in my Google Photos.  But I’ve been a loyal user for this app and it’s a very convenient and useful service. It beats paying for iCloud storage.

title: Just about perfect
content: Just about perfect. The GOOG Photos app has been the best mix of everything I'm looking for in an online photo backup service: every picture, every video I take is available anywhere, anytime on any device. Then neat extras--animations, movie compilations from content I shoot, and how the service organizes everything fits my needs to a tee. The app is reliable and fun to use. It's also dead-simple to learn. The fact that I don't HAVE to buy extra GOOG Drive storage & that the pictures I upload are in nearly full resolution works for me. I've done side-by-side comparisons with original photos and I can't tell any difference. Lastly, the search--holy cow, the search-- best in the business. I can type in almost any minute detail into the search bar & GOOG Photos finds what I'm looking for. Highly recommended.

title: stupid app
content: stupid app. i downloaded this app to look back at some cute photos i already have in my drive, but i figured that i don’t want all the photos i have on my phone to go into that google photos account, because it takes up SO much space. i need that space for a lot of stuff so i turned the backup OFF so new photos wouldn’t keep coming into the app, but next thing i know all the photos i take AFTER my backup is off are ON GOOGLE PHOTOS when i clearly said to NOT back them up? my icloud storage was running a bit low so i decided to use ANOTHER account that had no photos on it. so i switched to that account and i see ALL the photos from my phone on THAT account too, even when i never enabled backup for that account, LET ALONE ALL OF THEM! and this app is telling me, if i delete my photos from one account, it deletes it from all the other ones AND my phone WHEN i asked to NOT control my photos or back them up to the account? so i decided i’m never installing this app again because it’s so stupid and doesn’t even listen.

title: Loved it!
content: Loved it!. I got Google Photos on my phone to essentially replace the regular Photos since I liked the layout of Google Photos better. I haven’t had any issues since downloading it! It keeps my photos clean and well organized and the facial recognition software is 99% accurate. The only thing I would want more is maybe if they could add a feature where you could input more than one person in the search bar and come up with photos that had all of those people in them? Or maybe be able to search photos by date AND person. For example, inputting in the search bar “Max and Andy” could maybe come up with pictures of Max and Andy together. Or “Ruby 2020” comes up with pictures of Ruby taken in 2020? I just think that might be helpful. Anyway, overall I love this app!

title: 15 gigs??? Really???
content: 15 gigs??? Really???. Years ago i rated this app 5 stars…now…as of June 1st 2021, yall are lucky i gave you 2 stars like why on earth would you take away unlimited photo storage?? I have over 100,000 photos in my account, clearly I take a lot of pictures. I blow through the 15 gigs in 6 months or less and now I’m up to FIVE GOOGLE ACCOUNTS across all the photos/videos I’ve taken since june 1st 2021. You cheat me, I cheat you. This is such a pain and I’d rather not spend money on something I literally HAD. Maybe instead of making your Google Offices a “mental health playground” for your workers, let’s put that money towards the people who actually need to use your services. I’m not old enough to have a credit card, so it’s not even like I can pay for the storage if I wanted to. I am literally not capable of it. Please just bring back unlimited uploaded in High quality. I beg. Don’t get me wrong, the app WAS fantastic! My rating WAS 5 stars and I couldn’t thank you enough. But now, seriously y’all.

title: Amazing for more storage!!
content:
Amazing for more storage!!. Phenomenal app! I used to worry about my photos and videos taking my storage to, but Google Photos uses no storage after you safely back up all your photos to the app. After backing up your photos, you can delete them from your default app (like gallery or photos).
Google Photos is much different than the default app you may get on your phone. You can link certain photos to one face and search it up on the app. You will find every photo of that person on your device. 
Albums are extremely simple to create. The app will even suggest making a few for you when you take a lot of pictures in one location and time!
Another tool I love to use is looking up faces in your photos, like I mentioned before, and locations from your photos or even little things like searching the word “glasses” and it will show every picture in that place or with that object!
There are many other tools to help your photos, like filters for example. With the “assistant” tool you can see tips to help with your experience and little tweaks to your photos to make it pazzazed!!!
You can also make your own slideshow with FREE background music! It is so simple!
I’m so glad I use this app, it is so helpful and I hope you can use it successfully like I have!! :)

title: Great But Missing A Few Key Features For Super Users
content:
Great But Missing A Few Key Features For Super Users. I love google photos and have over 120,000 backed up, and pay for a terabyte every month; here are the main features I wish would be developed in the future.

- Sort photos by upload date (not only chronologically; if you have a lot photos and you want to see what photos for example you uploaded or backed up Jan 1, 2010... (but weren’t taken on Jan, 1, 2010) There is no easy way to do this, nor can you use the search bar for “uploaded Jan, 1 for this option.

- Tag Items; this would help with sorting or seeing with photos are in an album or not in an album. There’s no way to easily tell if a photo is not in any album at all. (I tagged) apple makes this easy with “hide photos” as you can hide the photos you add to a specific album... and work on the remainder. Tagging or being able to group specific screenshots (ie. work, school etc.) in the archive would be great as well.

- Upload from Google Backup to Specific Album. (You can do this on chrome if you drag and drop to the browser > add to album when upload is complete, but it can get stuck if too many items are pending; you cannot upload to specific album on the backup app itself.)

- Album view needs a small thumbnail to the left view option just like google drive, the album view is a little difficult to sort through if you have 50+ albums.

- Love Picasa so much and it’s a shame it’s no longer a google product that is used. Google Photos needs a similar desktop companion, the backup to drive/photos only option is an awkward and finicky app that Picasa was so much better than in my opinion.

title: I like it a lot
content: I like it a lot. At first, I had a hard time trying to figure it out but now I know what I’m doing and am especially glad I have google photos because two months ago I had to put my oldest cat to sleep. I was so depressed but with google photos I was able to make a movie with some of the photos I’d taken over the years of my cat. It has photos and video clips and music and I watch it often. I was able to save it and even download it to my iPhone and my iPad so that it isn’t just in the google photos app. I’m glad I have the google photos app because it is free unlike iCloud which expects you to pay after you’ve used up a certain amount of space. As soon as you access the google photos app it will back up all the most recent photos you’ve taken since you last accessed the app. If you are paying for iCloud space you might check out this app and be pleasantly surprised, I was.

title: Awesome UX
content:
Awesome UX. Where Apple dropped the ball with UX, Google picked it up and scored. Tremendously. 

I spent an hour trying to figure out how to backup the photos on my iPhone, and offload them from my phone. I used to upload them to my Mac via the Photos app, but that no longer works for some reason. I thought about upgrading iCloud but that seemed really confusing when trying to figure out how to share it with my wife.

I downloaded the Google Photos app and it was like BOOM, all problems solved within 2-3 taps. Backup? Yes. Offload from your phone and free up storage? Yes. Have a shared album space with my wife for all of our family photos? Yes and it was super easy.  Nailed it Google. You did your user research, identified the pain points, and made an awesome experience. And its unlimited storage for FREE! As long as you're okay with High quality!! Psh, no brainer!! Thank you Google!!! 👏👏👏👏👏

title: Better than iCloud Photos
content:
Better than iCloud Photos. I have been struggling for a couple of years with my Apple devices in terms of iCloud photo usage and syncing.  Seems like because of my slow internet speed and high number of pictures, iCloud just never worked out.  Never got all the photos to the cloud from my Mac, never got the photos that WERE on iCloud via my other devices BACK to the Mac quite in sync, and just a whole host of issues.  Even resorted to using high speed internet and dragging my Mac to hotels to use their wifi.  Still didn’t work out.

I finally opt for Google Photos and the associated Backup and Sync app and it just worked perfectly.  I used to eat up all my mobile hotspot data trying to get my Mac photos to the cloud (my only internet at home is via HotSpot).  While in a hotel I opted to try Google Photos and it took maybe 30 minutes tops for my entire collection to show up in Google Photos.  And I used the Google Photos app on my iPad as well and they both just work fine.  What’s even better is the ability to view my Google Albums on TV via the Roku channel View for Google Photos.

I can’t believe I struggled so long with such an easy solution.  I should have actually exported my Mac photos to albums in folder format so I could upload one album at a time to G Photos but nothing is perfect, yes it’s a little unorganized but I’ll get there and the G Photos assistant does a pretty nice job with recognition of places and people and things.

And I don’t have to shell out $2.99 a month either.  Got that warning from iCloud saying you may run out of space and have to increase storage and pay more....that was it for me and now I’m happy with Google Photos.  Not perfect but pretty darn close.

title: Store Pickup at Walgreens Didn’t Work
content: Store Pickup at Walgreens Didn’t Work. I was pleased that Google Photos offered the option to order photos for store pickup at Walgreens, as my daughter had some photos that she wanted printed urgently. She selected the photos, I placed the order, and I received a confirmation from Google Photos that the prints were ready. We went to Walgreens, and they had no record of my order. I showed them the confirmation message that verified that I had gone to the right Walgreens. They couldn’t help me and told me to place the order again using the Walgreens app, which I did. When I complained to Google Photos about my experience, they told me they couldn’t help me for orders placed in the store or using a kiosk — but the order was placed on Google Photos. I feel like I wasted time placing the order twice and being sent back and forth between Google Photos and Walgreens. It would be a nice option if it worked.

title: Thankful for google photos!
content: Thankful for google photos!. This app is great! Im not good with keeping phones, i have 5 kids and we are unfortunately very rough one devices. We lose, break and have occasional accidents that somehow factory reset phones & sadly I’m not great with technology. I love that Google photos can be set to automatically back up my photos & videos and how It allows me to add so much info about my pictures so I know where & when they were taken and on any kind of special of occasions bc that's a lot of hard work with 5 children. I’m super Thankful for google photos for helping me keep special & irreplaceable photos/vids! I can access them from any device, anytime and they make it effortlessly easy to share via social media, messages & email (etc.) & showing off my photos to our friends and family!

title: This is amazing
content: This is amazing. I was trying to see a way to free up space on my phone and it was my photos taking up all of my space so then on tiktok I saw this girl saying google photos is the best for it so when I downloaded it all I had to do is press one button (start backup) and then j could go on another app just not close the whole app and it would just start backing up my photos and so then when it’s done it will say all done and tell you to go to your actual photos app and press delete to all of them and I was nervous abt the idea but I still had all of my photos in one app ( google photos) I’m so glad I have this app it will also tell you if you might have some accident photos ( random screenshots or duplicates of photos) and then you can just delete them this app is truly a big help

title: Back up photos
content:
Back up photos. Love having a safe place to save all my photos that I’m not using at the moment, but don’t want to just erase them & be done either. I can have them automatically sync to my google
Photos from my iPhone & have it set up to only do certain albums like my “favorites” & that way I know all my pics in that album are safe & secure in my google photos & I may go to them & print, share, re-download them back on to my phone & much more if I so choose to. I’m so glad I stumbled across this by accident bc it’s gonna be 1 of those apps that when U get a new phone & u have that 1  group of apps that u can’t live without & u have to download asap bf U can even start using your phone, bc it looks & feels incomplete, unless u have that Handful of apps installed, well this app is now 1 of them in my group of apps like that!!💗💗THANKS GOOGLE😘😘

title: Best app ever!
content: Best app ever!. Saves so much storage in my phone and totally free (unless you want super high quality photos to be saved which doesn’t really matter for phone cams), and very user friendly! I have thousands of photos loaded into this app, and I haven’t experienced very many issues. The app does have a very difficult time handling larger videos, and can get crash when you make too many edits to multiple pictures, but other than that, pretty perfect! I think what would make this better is if I could organize albums into albums. I know it sounds weird, but when you have as many photos as me, you’ve got a bunch of albums to go along with them. It’d just be nice if I could group up certain albums in sections too, but it’s not too bad because you can search for the album names and people. Overall, really great app!

title: Love it!
content: Love it!. It’s incredible. I tell everyone about it. Free storage....gotta love that! iCloud makes you pay to keep the amount of photos I have.  Being able to take a pic on my cell and my tablet and access all my pics from either one..gotta love that! You can clear all your photos from other devices after you sync your pics to google photos. Frees up soo much space. I put old memory cards into my phone, sync it and am able to keep and see all my photos together. Google photos has Google assistant. Which has great features. Will make collages, gifs and videos for you all by itself. Some of the videos are hysterical. All the best parts of a video you took set to music. They do all the work for you!  I love it! They make videos with you and your children for Mother’s Day etc. So far I haven’t been disappointed..only impressed.

title: 10/10 Recommend
content: 10/10 Recommend. I was scared to use this app at first in fear I would loose all my photos, but now I have ten times the amount of my memories saved. I can view my pictures on all my devices since google is available anywhere nowadays! I have over 15,000 photos on my phone and it takes up less than half a gigabyte of space. I can easily share albums of photos I have taken to me and my friends. I do photography in my free time so this is so helpful for accessing my photos on my phone and on my computer. I recommend this to all my friends and family. Google also make collages, animations, and video montages of your pictures that you can save if you want. It is the simplest and most helpful app on my phone! No more running out of storage in the middle of a video. Anyways I hope you download this and genuinely enjoy it!!

title: STILL the best photo backup on iOS
content:
STILL the best photo backup on iOS. UPDATE: This is still the best photo album/backup app on the App Store. My only request would be for Google to add markup capabilities, especially on iPad. To be able to draw or write on my photos with the Apple Pencil would be amazing. Keep up the good work guys!

I’ve tried numerous photo backups on iphone, including photo stream/icloud, flickr, dropbox... This is the best, hangs down. Every complaint I ever had with those others has been addressed here. The addition of auto generating gifs and collages puts this one over the top for me. I haven’t even mentioned that they give you unlimited storage space! Absolutely ridiculous. I can’t say enough good things about it. Thanks google for another well thought out app that is incredibly useful. I wish Apple would utilize some of your ideas in their own software.

title: Saved all my images from my broken phone
content: Saved all my images from my broken phone. I saw this app on my galaxy s6and I thought of it the same way I Do when ever is see a random app that show up on my phone I didn’t really care about it but I saved it and that is the best thing I did ... but one Friday last week when I was going to school I tried to turn on my phone it won’t then when I got to school I tried to charge it nothing then I knew it I lost the most important things to me my pictures, the last photo of the dog who got hit by a car following my other, the first time I seen snow, car spotting, and pictures of my current dog... title: Fantastic - should have been using this years ago
content: Fantastic - should have been using this years ago. I explored a lot more f different apps and was overly worried about photo quality.  In retrospect, I should have just gone to google photos right out of the gate.  Quality is top notch (even on the free setting) for everyone short of those with extremely high end cameras - for the rest of us google’s base quality is higher than our phones can generate anyway.  The real kicker is how it makes your photos accessible and useful.  The assistant regularly creates albums that are of interest and keeps “memories alive” by doing it.  The ability to search photos is phenomenal.  I had a crazy number of photos on my phone but never looked at them for years - we’ve gone through them more in the last 6 months with google photos than we ever would have otherwise.  Highly recommended.

title: BEST APP EVER!!!
content:
BEST APP EVER!!!. If you are a picture fan like me, (well over 50,000 pics taken a saved 🤷🏽‍♀️🤦🏽‍♀️) then this app is hands down the BEST! All pictures get backed up instantly without you having to do a thing! The “assistant” feature even makes collages, mini videos, albums and more, again without you having to do anything! You can even “drag and drop” pictures from a desktop or laptop right into the Google Photos web page. It’s beyond amazing! You can create your own albums and organize your photos YOUR WAY. No more need to purchase flash drives or external memory systems as Google Photo is 100% free and has unlimited storage! 🙌🏽 That’s a big deal for me. 
I never write reviews but there was no way I was going to pass on this one. Thank you Google for letting me keep my pictures of my girls, my family and friends safe and sound!! 👍🏽

title: Automated collages, videos, and animations 👌🏽
content:
Automated collages, videos, and animations 👌🏽. Endless storage is my favorite thing about google photos!
Google could have stopped there, but the amazement doesn’t stop there!
A couple weeks ago was my sons 3rd birthday. Somehow google found all the pix of my son I’d taken over the past three years, but only the best ones (there weren’t any duplicated photos not even the 5 or 6 you take trying to get a good one) and created a “they grow up so fast” slide show, complete w music 🎶 
I’d been meaning to put together one myself, but the amount of time it takes to do so was discouraging me from actually starting to do it.  But Google went ahead and did it for me 😁 What a time saver!!
Only thing is I wish they would have completed it sooner so I could have posted it on the day of his bday, rather than days later. Still awesome though!!

title: Easy accessible storage
content:
Easy accessible storage. I’m happy to have google photos mainly because I know that if my phone gets lost , broken or stolen  that my photos will be stored in my account. Even now having an Apple phone I have no problem accessing or saving my photos to Google Photos. 

I also like that I can have Google photos sort my pictures by who is in them. The facial recognition feature is very good. The suggestions Google photo offers to archive certain things is helpful and time saving for me. 

I really love all the special features like how Google Photos will make a video of a certain person or certain date or show other suggestions of how to do cool things with your photos. I always get excited to watch and see what memories Google photo chooses to use in the videos, etc.

title: The BEST
content: The BEST. I’ve been using this app for yeaarsss and never had a problem... my son passed away passed away almost 4 years ago and I have all his photos and videos saved on google photos and I know I can go back and look or make collages or videos of his pictures anytime.. I can even rider things like cups or shirts with his pictures on them!! It’s the best app ever and I know I can always depend on GOOGLE PHOTOS to keep my pictures and videos safe!! I’ve had my pictures on google since I had my first son in 2004 and they are still there!!! LOVE IT AND I RECOMMEND THIS APP TO ANY AND EVERYONE!! I’m just a normal person from Myrtle beach South Carolina I didn’t get paid or promised anything from anybody to make this review.. I just thought I would share my opinion for others so they know they can trust this app!!! That is GOOGLE for another great app you provide its awesome sauce lol

title: Love this app but….
content:
Love this app but….. It works as advertised. So easy to sync with your Google account and have your pictures uploaded automatically. Just turn on when I lay down for bed and it uploads all the pictures to my Google account.
BUT I dont like the fact that I can’t easily download my photos to my computer and not have all the metadata date etc with them. I understand that google wants to charge for storage but I should have the right , the ability to get my photos as I uploaded them. I’m moving I will continue to use the backup feature of google photos until I fill my 100 gigabytes but I’m using another site and I’m also making sure they are backed up on my hard drive so I have full control. 
I got sucked in while google was offering unlimited storage. Shame on them and shame on me for not realizing what they were doing.

title: Thank goodness for Google Photos
content: Thank goodness for Google Photos. I found myself in the same situation many of you do. My phone was running out of memory and my pictures were at risk of being lost forever. Then I was told about Google Photos, so I downloaded it and set it for auto backup. I had priceless pictures on my phone of my mom and dad, who have both now moved on to heaven. These pictures could never be captured again. Then the day came. No choice but to get a new phone. Imagine how relieved I was to find ALL of my photos from the old phone waiting for me in Google Photos right on my new device. Thanks Google for protecting my priceless memories forever! If you don’t have this yet... don’t delay another second. Your priceless memories once gone can never be recalled again. You will be so thankful you got Google Photos and protected those memories forever!

title: Double Trouble
content:
Double Trouble. Edit: It is January 1st, 2018 and of course, for the new year I have taken many pictures. I check the pictures so I can start backing them up and honestly I’ve had it. New year, new app lol. I don’t want to see any more pictures being multiplied and I will be switching apps. 

Old review: is For many this problem is nonexistent, but there are a few, like me, who experience it daily. The problem is having pictures being uploaded twice to google photos. Almost every single time I back up my photos they show up twice. With that being said, I could be uploading over 1000 photos but it  shows up as 2000 because it multiples every single picture. Only solution is to manually delete one of them, but one picture is the original and the other is a rendered quality or filtered for some reason and you have to first notice which one is the one you want and then delete the other. This is very time consuming and irritating. Other than that, it is a great app that I use every day. I would just love if that problem would go away.

title: Don’t Get This App!!
content: Don’t Get This App!!. Look, I know what you’re thinking. “There are so many good reviews this app must be great since it’s run through Google, right?” Wrong. I thought the same thing when I was downloading this app. It deletes your photos from the Photos app, makes you PERMANENTLY delete them, then doesn’t even save fast if you want to transfer them back into the Photos app on your phone. I downloaded this app to help clear my iCloud storage and let me tell you, it did not change a single thing. The storage didn’t free up at all, and I’ve just struggled. I’ve currently been trying to redownload my pictures to my phone and it keeps replying with “turn on the internet to download photos” even though I have full WiFi bars and Cellular Data on for the app. I have 600+ photos that I want to transfer from this app to my iCloud photos, and it won’t let me. Doesn’t even save a singular photo unless I want to wait five hundred million hours. So unless you plan on experiencing what I just did, I would not download this app.

title: Great app but…
content:
Great app but…. I upgraded my google one to a paid service to take advantage of all the photo editing tools that was just released for ios recently, esp the Magic eraser tool…but I don’t see any of the enhanced tools available for all my photos. Not really sure what they are marketing when its not an available service. Planning just to try out the service to see if its even worth keeping since none of the tools marketed for paid service is even available. Will update post if things change but right now its ok. 

Update: 3/2/23
After I wrote the review somehow the google photos app suddenly has the tools option. Works great, though not perfect but it def works well. Will keep my subscription for now since it has all the photo editing tools I’ve been wanting.

title: Could be better
content:
Could be better. In general, the automatic back up seems good, although I have noticed that a lot of my photos have not made it into the Google database.  The trouble is, I have no way of knowing which of my historical photos were successfully transported in which were not, without a one to one review which could take days.

The search function is very useful, though by no means perfect. The facial recognition is also suspect. I know I have scores and scores of photos of a particular individual saved, but only seven made it into the folder marked for that person.

You can take an unusually long time to back up a photo, and an equally unreasonable amount of time to download and save photo back onto your device. I wish the whole thing would act more quickly.

Finally, I wish albums would be stored alphabetically so that you could more easily find the album you were looking for when you want to add photos to it. As it is, you have a disorganized list of albums which very quickly becomes quite lengthy And you speed needless time trying to find the album that you want. This is made more complicated by the fact that Google photos creates its own albums with names that are not what you would have given them.

All in all, a good app that could be better, and perhaps it is the best currently available.

title: Ordering photo prints for delivery doesn’t work!!
content: Ordering photo prints for delivery doesn’t work!!. I have so many years of photos in Google Photos. I selected many photos to print and have delivered to me. They didn’t come on the scheduled delivery date so I reached out to Google. They said I had to wait an additional two weeks. At the end of the two weeks my photos hadn’t arrived so I called Google again. The representative attempted to talk me into getting them reordered. I said no way because you couldn’t get them to me the first time so why should I expect you can deliver them on a second order. The representative kept pressing me to reorder and I finally said that I wanted a full refund of the three separate orders immediately. It was like pulling teeth to get my money back. However, once the refunds were issued I had my money in two days. I have precious memories that I wanted hard prints of so I’m moving forward with a different option for printing my memories. If you order prints, I wish you good luck! Donna H.

title: Hate this app
content: Hate this app. I have to have this app only bc this is how my family shares photos but it’s just so bad and awful to use. You can’t fully turn off back up function on iPhone it will still be linked to backed up photos so when you try to delete backed up photos in the app it deletes from the device too even if you have back up turned off. So stupid and infuriating had to delete the app and manage from the website. Creating an album is such a pain half the time it doesn’t work you literally have to go thru and re-select all the photos you want to add several times for them to finally upload. It saves a COPY of a photo you want to edit vs giving you the option to replace the original this creates an additional image in your phone which throws it off of the original order you had the photos in these are small things but so inconvenient there are smaller name apps with miles better functionality and none of the hassle this app is trash to say the least.

title: Best photo organization/storage app
content:
Best photo organization/storage app. Just log into your Google account, take pictures as you normally would, and the app helps you store and access all the pictures taken on the phone. This is especially useful when I switch to a new phone, just log into Google account on new phone and bam! Instant access to all your photos taken with old phone. 

You can also search through your photos with the search bar. If you try looking up “car,” it’ll go through all your photos that have a car in the photo. It can even recognize some peoples faces. Doesn’t work all the time but this is definitely another great feature.

Only con I see is that you used to get unlimited storage but they're charging people for more storage after 50gb

title: Great product, but won’t upload everything
content:
Great product, but won’t upload everything. I LOVE this app! Love how I can keep my photos, everything no matter what happens to my phone. I love I can find groups of pictures using a date, name, or face! I love how easy it is to use. I LOVE the “assistant” too! The assistant makes animations from photos, stylizes photos, makes great videos from my photos! And I LOVE how it takes a look back, 1 or more years on the same day—so nice to see! The only thing I wish I could change is that I WISH I could change the order of the photos I choose to make an animation! For some reason I can choose which photos, but not the order! I could make the animation flow better to my liking. Alas I don’t use that option as much because of this, even though it’s a great tool.

Update: there are several photos and videos that won’t upload to the website. I have tried everything. That’s pretty frustrating.

title: This app solves all the problems you may have experienced with “iCloud photo storage”
content: This app solves all the problems you may have experienced with “iCloud photo storage”. Honestly love this app!!! Makes storing my photos without taking up space soooo simple and effective. I also enjoy some of the edits the “assistant” puts out. Definitely recommend to any apple people out there, since iCloud storage is completely stupid. The layout took me a little bit to get used to but it’s easier than you think. It also has this amazing archive feature that lets you store unwanted or what I use it for is more silly pictures not on your home dashboard! If you’re on the edge just try it and you’ll fall in love. My only recommendation is that you could make a feature to set wallpapers directly from the app instead of re-saving it to normal photos and doing it from there. But still overall amazing app!!!

title: I do like this app.
content:
I do like this app.. This app is super helpful to me. I have a lot of pictures/memories. This application has helped me get them more organized than they were. 
There are things that I wish I had more control over, access to. Ways to edit, put together for projects, different photos. Something’s the app does to photos on its own to show me as feature photos that I wish I could do myself threw the app. Example-make color pop photos, collages, etc. Obviously the program can accomplish these things but as an user I’m not able to access the features for my own use or haven’t figured out how. I’m sure there’s a reason why ($$$)
Just not sure if my ability to design things out of my own pictures should be “x”ed out because of a lack of financial means. My thoughts not accusations.
I really appreciate the app just the same!

title: Love the assistant!
content: Love the assistant!. This app is easily one of my favorite apps, it lets me clean up my phones photo album while not having to make tough choices on what to delete and what to keep because this app keeps it all for me!! If I ever need to add a pic back into my photo album for a throwback post on social media I can just pop in and quickly save it to my camera roll. I also LOVE the assistant - it will randomly send me reminders for throwback pictures and I so enjoy seeing things from “this day 5 years ago” for example. It also makes you movies and applies awesome filters - I’m always excited to see what google photos assistant has come up with when I get a notification - it makes photo storage so much fun. And I am someone who doesn’t really trust technology lol but google photos has my trust and I recommend it to everyone I know!!!

title: Very reliable and trusty photo storing app.
content: Very reliable and trusty photo storing app.. I really enjoy the set up this app gives me. It keeps my pictures organized by date, and it saves every photo in my gallery I really enjoy that, there’s only one real downside about this app (that I'm almost positive will be improved) is how when you delete a photo off your gallery sometimes it tends to delete off google photos unless you’ve opened google photos before you deleted the picture from your normal gallery. Still a 5 star app I’ve learned to open before deleting off my regular gallery, would really be a great advancement especially since I have to allow access to the app to my photos when first downloaded. Again overall a fantastic app! Thank you google you saved a lot of photos on my gallery when my phone was destroyed.!!! LIFE SAVER!!! All day. You da bomb

title: An essential app!
content: An essential app!. I hope the unlimited photos feature of this service never changes! I will forever use this app to store all my photos. Not only is it good for backup but also good for making albums and sharing pictures with other people. My friends and I will also make a collaborative album where we all put in pics from a recent road trip or an even that we’ve had together and be able to see photos from all different perspectives at one place. The ability to share one’s entire gallery of photos is also a great feature if you have a family member or spouse that you can just give access to for photos and they won’t have to wait for you to share it with them manually every time you have new pics! Overall, Google Photos is the best way to go! I recommend this to anyone

title: The Best...
content:
The Best.... There are numerous apps, many different clouds, and several other ways for us all to store and manage our photos....They all pale in comparison to google photos, however...From the features, to the amount of space offered, no other comes close to meeting the prestigious standards or reaching the impressively high bar that google has set with this app. Bravo Google!

Update: My only complaint is that the photo assistant would initially make a ton of great and interesting suggestions and always had some cool animations to surprise me with, but that had almost came to a complete halt!😧 Is there maybe a setting that I’ve overlooked that could increase this near the way that it was in the beginning? If not, I think that would be a cool addition...Other than that, I still Love what y’all have done with it...Keep it up! XD

title: Poor app update
content: Poor app update. I am a longtime user of Google Photos, and the new update is disappointing. In the past, photos were clearly sorted by date for easy visual reference while scrolling through the feed. It used to be very easy to see what day a photo or group of photos was taken because there was a clear date header, and it was easy to select all photos from a given date simultaneously if desired. Unfortunately, now the photos all appear as one large group with no differentiation other than a date changing rapidly at the top of the feed as you scroll up or down. The new layout is disorganized, looks cluttered (especially for users with a large number of photos), and is much less user friendly. The only way I can truly see where one day ends and another begins now is to open up each photo’s metadata one at a time until I come to the next day. This is time consuming and defeats the purpose of a photo organization app. I hope the former layout will be restored.

title: Learning curve
content: Learning curve. I purchased extra storage space from Google. I made the mistake of assuming it was going to Google for safe keeping. Yet every time I send photos to storage it’s putting them in my iCloud account. This is not why I pay for storage. However I could be mistaken and I may be doing something wrong. No matter, it shouldn’t be this difficult and Google shouldn’t be vague on how or why thing’s don’t gel. This could be all my fault, or not. I’m new to Google photos and I understand that a learning curve is a prerequisite in life. But it shouldn’t be so hard to get answers. For instance, it won’t let me view my photos that they suggest to delete to make space on whatever place they send them to. Not clear or reasonable explanation for this either. Google are you listening? I’m not going to trash my lifelong photos just because you say so. I want to see for myself before I delete anything! Good luck folks, I hope your much more savvy than I am.

title: Bait & switch + No way to sort by size
content:
Bait & switch + No way to sort by size. Nice bait and switch by getting us hooked to the “free backups” of lower quality sizes, but then putting a 15gb cap. That cap is reached in days and then they stop you from sending and receiving email until you are under the cap. Holding you hostage until you pay. No thanks! Ain’t gonna work on me. I will just go delete the biggest items until under the limit, and stop backing up new items. 

This leads to the second issue. There is no way to sort items by size. At all.  Not even in non-mobile versions. You can’t list by details or any other sorting methods that should be available. This missing feature which should be considered a basic feature is likely missing so you can’t easily get under the 15gb free tier. They are trying to get you to just give up and pay for storage (that used to be free for lower quality remember). Well no thanks. Tip for others in the same dilemma: just find the list of just videos and go and delete the longest ones.

title: 15,000 photo storage and better than iCloud
content: 15,000 photo storage and better than iCloud. Well 15,000 is a number when a average photo is 8,000,000bits or 1,000,000 bytes or 1,000 kigabytes or 1 megabyte or .001 gigabytes. Okay you get the point. I can have all my devices that has internet to vein them and any device with a camra and internet to take photos. The photos are on the phone you can delete because there all in google photos.  Phone transfers are easy to just sign in to the account and you got all your photos there. Best of art is it’s 15mbs free forever and you can upgrade. This device is cheaper than iCloud. Google photos tripled iCloud free storage. All they need to to is make the app for Apple TV and then it will be the best photo app ever. You can even edit the photo color, draw, reangle it and more. You can easy take a photo off of google photos and move it where ever.

title: Great app; needs Apple TV port
content:
Great app; needs Apple TV port. March 2020 Update: I still love Google Photos. One thing it *definitely* needs is a Share Sheet extension so I can be in a 3rd Party app (Eg WhatsApp) and still access my Google Photos pictures. This would make it 5 stars. You can already do this from iMessage because of the Google Photos iMessage extension. We need a similar function from WhatsApp, Messenger, etc. 

Original review:
Google photos is a great app for doing what it's designed: photo backup and retrieval. It backs up your entire photo library and allows you to view it on the web or anywhere that supports a Google photos app. My 1 star deduction is because it lacks an Apple TV app to easily view photos directly on your TV. Once I delete old photos from my phone the only way to view photos on my TV is to view them in google photos on my iPhone and AirPlay the screen. This needs a better approach.

title: Disappointing
content: Disappointing. I just wasted 2 hours of my time selecting photos to add to an album. First of all, when I zoom in to a picture with the button in the bottom right, it is an automatic reflex for me to press the X in the top left to exit the zoom in. But no, that just reset me after I had selected about 300 photos. How about adding a safety questions “Are you sure you want to exit this album?” Secondly, when I was finally able to finish selected 500 photos to create an album, I created it and it was fine. Then I go to my home screen and when I return, the album is gone, not in the trash bin, not in the archive, it just disappeared and I couldn’t recover it. This was already frustrating enough but somehow I convinced myself to try again. 500 photos, I leave the app, comeback, 12 photos in the album I just created. I don’t know what kind of garbage this is, but I just wasted 2 hours just to not even be able to do something as simple as create an album. Thanks a lot, looks like i’ll be deleted this app 2 hours after getting it.

title: NOT A FAN OF THE LATEST FEATURE
content:
NOT A FAN OF THE LATEST FEATURE. If Google Photos didn’t recently start automatically saving photos to your library that people send you on Messenger, no doubt I would’ve given 5 stars! I did on my last review.
Keep in mind, I haven’t looked into it yet to see if this feature can be disabled but I hope so! And for a few reasons...
#1 - personally, I don’t necessarily WANT TO SAVE EVERY random photo someone else decides to send you!
#2 - see #1 and with unlimited storage you get with Google Photos that can add to an already HUGE collection, adding to the amount of time it’s now going to take to sort through all those extra photos 
#3 - see #2 regarding taking more time to sort through photos - photos (or jokes, screenshots, etc) that may not be appropriate for every person you allow access to your Google Photos (or access to your devices with it installed) 
#4 - see #1-3 potentially inappropriate or offensive photos are saved ONCE THEY ARE SENT! NOT EVEN VIEWED! So if you’re like me & don’t go on messenger often, you could have photos saved from days or weeks before you even realize it!
PLEASE consider doing away with this feature, everything else about this app is awesome! But I don’t think this feature was very well thought out prior to implementing it. And if there is a way to disable, PLEASE SOMEONE LET ME KNOW!

title: Genuinely my best download of all time
content: Genuinely my best download of all time. I bought google photos back when i was entering my 6th grade (i’m college freshman now) it has been my best download because it is the ONLY reason i have access to all of my memories from then every single thing that i ever put in my camera roll saved itself- it’s genuinely miraculous. i’ve had multiple phone swaps i would back it up and it would always lose footage but then one time i had a failed backup lost everything i forgot about google photos for a while I hopped on and it was all there, quite literally the best time capsule you could ever have, if you’re a parent reading this do your kids the favor install it for them they won’t remember these little things and maybe even have it. genuinely so grateful

title: Praise and Requests
content: Praise and Requests. Very good app, incredibly helpful for saving space on your phone. However, there are a few things I’d like to have added. I’d like to be able to delete a photo from within an album. It allows me to remove the photo from the album, but not delete it. I’d also like to be able to star any photos or videos i like in particular, and have it automatically added to an album as soon as I star it. It’s very quick, and less easy to forget. Sometimes I forget to add something to an album, so starring it would be much quicker. Preferably I’d like to increase the photo maximum for albums, but that’s not a huge deal. Overall, while there of course can be improvements, the app is very good. Allows me to keep more things on my phone, while still collecting photos and videos. I love the tips assistant, having it suggest collages and stylized photos. Very nice app.

title: Google Photos
content:
Google Photos. I have enjoyed Google Photos and being able to see all the photos my daughter posts and put them in my camera roll so I can see them daily whenever I choose! This is so important to me! My grandboys are my darling boys my treasure and it is nice to have photos daily of them! I also love interior decor and beautiful homes and friends have been gracious to share photos that I love to look at daily! I’m not sure what I’m going to do now! I’m trying to do better in removing photos and I need to put photos in books!

March 10, 2023
I still enjoy Google Photos!!
I will be deleting photos from ICloud or somewhere to give me more space until I can get a new phone that has more storage space! Sorry I’m so slow to do this. It takes a lot of time to delete!

title: A Godsend
content:
A Godsend. I’m so grateful for google photos. The AI videos and stuff are next level. The search capabilities in photos are otherworldly.I literally took a picture of a recipe on paper about five years ago and didn’t think of it sense. I literally looked up some of the words that I knew were written on the recipe and Google brought it up. What?! I am still in awe over that one.

You are one of few companies that massive that actually regards user experience over profits. There are a lot of companies that directly intersect with yours that are only about updating and upselling products with some of the most non-user-friendly features ever. It’s crazy to be revered and have a total lack of positive user experience in areas. You are the gold standard.

You care about the experience and it shows. Your audience is grateful.

title: poorly designed
content: poorly designed. i started with google photos to separate my i-cloud photos from others, free up storage, and share business photos with clients. it worked fine through web browser but was super clunky downloading from i-cloud then up-loading to google photos. so i got the app to speed that up. then the app forced me to give it full access to my photos, and whether or not i allow backups, it syncs to my icloud and uploads and deletes across both platforms no matter what. WHAT A STUPID DESIGN!!! why the f can’t i just delete stuff within the google app and choose what it can access/control in i-cloud? why do i have to give it full access? why must it show my entire phone’s photo/video album? i already have it right here. i need a separate app to do separate things. it seems you’re so focused on it making it do stupid slideshows and other annoying gimmicks i don’t even want that you’re missing the whole reason i do want it.

title: EXCELLENT!! 100/5 if I could!
content:
EXCELLENT!! 100/5 if I could!. I went FULLY from phone backing up pics/vids to backing them over WiFi using Google Photos; it NEVER disappoints! Unlimited pics backups and couple of GBs for vids backup. I saved LOTS of space on my iPhone. I also LOVE the suggestions whether to share pics w/ people that is recognize their faces accurately, and suggestions to build GIF or grid of images out of the uploaded pics! I love how it organizes your screenshot clutter those shots which includes lots of texts suggesting to archiving. Finally, not to forget to mention grouping pics based on timeframe and/or group of or specific people, let alone the amazing functionality of the search function within the app as well as editing pic/vid if you like.

Not worried at all about privacy issues knowing Google’s highest privacy standards and complex security algorithms they use in general let alone those implemented in Google Photos as well as the advanced Artificial Intelligence algorithms used in face recognition of vids in pics!

5/5 easily!!!! actually 100 over 5 if I can. A happy Google customer loving how they always thrive to accomplish the very best in ALL of their services to reach highest levels of customers/end users satisfaction.

Keep it up Google, and keep it up you guys! 

-Arwa

title: Life Changing
content:
Life Changing. I wanted to try Google Photos forever before I finally did because I was so afraid of storing all my pictures in the cloud. I can’t even remember why. Maybe I was worried about the security of it, or maybe I thought it would somehow be complicated or inconvenient. 

It’s hard to imagine why I wouldn’t have wanted this, though, because it’s a no brainer to me now. Using this has cleared up a ton of space on my phone (it’s an iPhone 6 that only has 16GB of storage, yet I can always download everything I want to). 

It has also allowed me to consolidate my semi-recent pictures (since having a phone at all) and my old ones from the digital camera I used to use. The convenience of being able to access all of my pictures anytime, anywhere is phenomenal. 

The app is also incredibly user-friendly, as is the desktop site. And I love how well it recognizes and compiles both people and pets, not to mention locations. 

This app makes my life easier, more convenient, more organized, more streamlined in general. I absolutely love it, I’ve been using it for months now, and I can’t imagine ever ceasing to use it. 

Yet another all-around success from Google that pushes me one step closer to choosing them over Apple for my next phone.

title: still the best app overall to save and document all of your photos
content:
still the best app overall to save and document all of your photos. Google Photos has been the cornerstone of my digital memory bank since 2006. The app’s intuitive interface and cutting-edge face recognition technology stand out, making it a breeze to sift through years of cherished family moments. 

Whether I’m reminiscing about the past or searching for a specific person, Google Photos delivers with remarkable precision.
What truly sets it apart is its user-friendly design, ensuring that every memory is just a few clicks away. 
For anyone looking to safeguard their precious moments, I can’t recommend Google Photos highly enough. as long as you safeguard your Google app with two factor authentication then your Google Photos account should be relatively safe.

title: Love this app!!
content: Love this app!!. Over the years I've lost too many pictures. With this app it saves all my pictures, from all my devices. Sometimes it's too good, in that it also saves the crap ones that need deleted ha ha Ha but that's OK I rather have some extra crap ones than lose any good ones. Everyone should have this app! UPDATE: my opinion hadn’t changed. I go through and delete now, since I do pay the $20 a year since I’ve used up my free storage (for 20 gig I think it is? 100 gig? I don’t even know) and the next level is a way higher price as of now. I don’t really blame them for charging, and it’s a reasonable fee. For now. I do worry about some kind of global EMP wiping out everything, but that’s my personal paranoia and I can print if I’m really that worried. I keep meaning to do that…🤪

title: Overall great, but pictures are dull
content:
Overall great, but pictures are dull. Overall the app works great and I’ve been using it for years. However, I’ve noticed recently after switching to IOS that there is a very start difference in image quality when viewing the same picture in the IOS Photos app and the Google Photos app on my iPhone. I think this is due to the “view in HDR” setting in IOS photos. If you view the same picture in both apps, it will appear to have much more dynamic range with better contrast and highlights. 

HDR videos appear identical across both apps, so the issue looks to be exclusive to viewing photos within Google Photos. 

Note: If I delete the photos from my device, then download it to my device from Google Photos, it appears expected in the IOS Photos app, so it’s not an issue if any compression or anything, just for how they are displayed in the Google Photos app

title: Amazing Organization
content:
Amazing Organization. I’ve used google photos for years now, and it has DEFINITELY made my photos easier to find and organize. It automatically identifies what is in a given photo, so if I want to look for a picture of a car, I can simply search car and see only pictures that feature cars! I also love the memories feature, as I get to see pictures from a year or two ago today :)

I’ve also had to upload a lot of pictures for school with online school this past year, and google photos automatically saves my pictures from my camera roll onto the cloud, which means I can take a picture with my phone and simply pull up the website on my computer, and the picture is already up! Saves SO much time and energy!

title: Great app!
content: Great app!. Great app! Google Photos is amazing, once you upload all your photos from apple photos or any other type of photo storage you get 15 more GB for photos. I have a IPhone and you only get 5 GB for your entire iCloud storage for everything, unless you want to pay monthly for storage which I didn’t like so much. Google photos styluses your photos if you choose to do so and makes the photo look great, it even makes it’s own animations out of everything you took videos out of; that feature is awesome! You can make your own book out of every photo you own which is great for family photo books and you can access all of your stored photos and videos on any device! All in All this offers everything Apple Photos does and way more! If you own a apple phone you should own Google Photos! :)

title: Was okay, has issues
content:
Was okay, has issues. I switched to another service since google went to a paid subscription. I had this for a few years and have noticed a big problem trying to download things out of google photos.

- If you have mixed media types of Live Photos, Videos, and non-live photos you cannot save any mix of them at once. You MUST save live photos, videos and normal photos all separately otherwise it can’t save them.

- If you have slow-mo videos I was unable to download them from google photos after they have been there for 2 years.

The hay that broke the camel’s back though… when you use google photos you are accepting that they can train their AI to recognize objects and people. They say it’s private, but from their track record I doubt it is. This wouldn’t be a problem, but now that it is a paid service I don’t agree that I have to pay for them to use my photos to train their AI.

The biggest down side besides privacy concerns with the AI training, when you upload photos and videos they need to be scanned by the AI fully before you can download it back from google photos or use the person finder feature. You cant add photos yourself to a person you must wait for the AI to do this. This process can take months or even years for it to complete depending on how many photos/videos you have, it doesn’t tell you what ones have or haven’t been scanned, and there is no priority list it’s all random.

While it backs photos up fine, and has features that are nice to have. The issues above are pretty bad, it took me almost a full week moving my photos and videos and I was unable to get a few of the videos, thankfully not super important ones.

title: Best photos app other than recent bugs
content: Best photos app other than recent bugs. Overall, I love this app. It has so many awesome features like the incredible search engine. You can literally search for text in a photo and it will find it! This is extremely handy. It has unbelievable face recognition and can recognize an adult and child as being the same person! Of course, the sharing capabilities are great too. However, recently it has started crashing all of the time and locking up. I can’t even use it now because it crashes within seconds every time. I have the latest iOS, latest Google photos update, etc. but it does it every time. I hope this is fixed soon because it is useless now. The only other idea for improvement would be to improve Apple photos compatibility. Like allowing your Apple albums to show in your Google photos. And allowing captions would be nice too.

title: Great App but Google's Killing it.
content:
Great App but Google's Killing it.. UPDATE: Google just announced they would be getting rid of the unlimited uploads in June 2021. This basically makes the app useless for me. I don't have a lot of money to spend on Google One, and Google estimated that I would run out of storage within a year. It looks like I'm going to remove it after June. It's no longer the savior of photo storage, but just another cloud storage app. Really disappointed.

Old Review: I found out about Google Photos last year and have been loving it! I am a photographer, and I have an older phone with 16gigs of storage, so I was trying to find a way to store photos I take with my camera so that I could show them to friends. But that tiny amount of storage on my phone made that impossible.

This would still be the case even if I had a phone with 256GB. I need that storage for other things, such as other apps, not full 25 megapixel photos. If I'm just showing friends photos on my phone screen, or them texting to them, I don't need that massive file.
So the shrinking is a bonus. A smaller file to put on social media or text to people, all while having all my photos in the palm of my hand and on any other device that has internet.
Even if you are an actual photographer and not just a smartphone shutterbug, I highly recommend this app.

content:
Awesome App!!. Super easy to use, very convenient. It really takes all if the hassle and hard work out of having to save photons and documents and move them around. You can share with CONTACTS, you can EDIT PHOTOS, and easily access all of your information from any device with an internet connection.

title: Google Photos is excellent!
content: Google Photos is excellent!. Google Photos does the little extras I don’t generally have time for in my busy life. The Google photo assistant processes your photos with special effects or compiles animations and slideshows from your photos. Then, it sends you a notification to review and either save or delete its suggestions. It’s like getting a special little gift or treat on my phone. Having Google photos paired with Google Drive on my phone puts the ability to organize and save what’s important to me right at my fingertips and ensures that I won’t lose any precious memories. The entire suite of Google applications (Slides, Docs, Sheets...) has become an invaluable set of easy-to-use and easy-to-share tools that I access daily for important personal life-interests as well as to augment workflows and communication on the job.

title: Shockingly Bad Privacy and Sharing Design
content:
Shockingly Bad Privacy and Sharing Design. Google Photos has one of the most poorly designed and opaque sharing systems I have ever encountered in a consumer app. That this comes from Google is honestly unbelievable.

There is no clear or authoritative way to see which specific photos are shared with which people at any given time. Instead, sharing is scattered across partner sharing, shared albums, backup state, and receiver-side behavior that the sender cannot see or verify. As a user, you are left guessing about who can access deeply personal photos and whether deleting them actually revokes that access.

The app completely fails to explain basic, critical questions:
• Are shared photos view-only or copied into another person’s library?
• Can recipients retain photos permanently outside the sender’s control?
• What exactly does deletion revoke, and what does it not?
• Who can see what right now?

This is not a minor UX issue. It is a fundamental privacy transparency failure. Users should not have to rely on Reddit threads, experimentation, or panic to understand the consequences of sharing their own photos.

Apple’s Photos app clearly labels shared versus private content and makes access obvious. Google Photos does the opposite, creating confusion, anxiety, and real loss of trust.

For a company that constantly claims to prioritize privacy, this design is unacceptable. Until Google provides a single, clear view showing exactly who has access to which photos, Google Photos does not deserve user confidence.

title: It’s magical!
content: It’s magical!. The facial recognition is amazing and it’ll group your photos by person (and pet)! You can also search your photos for random things like trees, clouds, mountains, etc. and it does a fantastic job pulling up all those things. It’ll read the tagging on your photos so you can search for locations too. All these things help you search for the photos you want to see very quickly. Of course don’t forget that by uploading your photos to Google you are basically putting them all in cloud storage and you basically have a backup... or delete them from your device for more room and instead just access them from the cloud. Finally it’ll occasionally take your photos and auto-create movies/stylized photos/animations/collages/virtual albums/etc. and the results are pretty cool.

title: The Best Thing Ever!
content: The Best Thing Ever!. I love to take pictures, but phones come with various problems with that. One, they take too much space, two, there isn’t enough room for them, three, I can view them on one device and never see them again after my phone gives out, and four, I can never find the time to edit the photos or find good editing tools. However, this app fixes EVERYTHING! It’s a game-changer. It even creates movies, animations, and memory books for free! Now that’s only a bonus to the program! You can view it on any device, it takes almost no room, can store millions of photos, and it styles, edits, designs, and sorts all the photos for you! Another bonus is you can search up the place, year, or person in the photo and get accurate results! Now pinch me to make sure I‘m not dreaming!

title: I wish I’d known about it sooner
content:
I wish I’d known about it sooner. Google Photos is the best way I’ve found to store and backup my phone’s pictures. It’s simple, intuitive and painless. The Assistant’s suggestions, albums and photo edits are fun and surprisingly good. The only problems stem from having to have internet access to show off snaps, and the need to reimport pics to the Photo Roll in order to use them in other apps (for example, avatars for social media or contacts). 
I also use it for my laptop, but as I haven’t verified that it stores all the metadata from each picture (as many others don’t), I’ve yet to transition my “good” DSLR pictures here exclusively. 
I’d love to see a function whereby certain folders would NOT be removed from my phone after archiving, as this would help immensely with pictures I take and need for work.

title: Google photos
content: Google photos.
