Ultimately, google photos is great for reassuring yourself that all of your photos and videos are safe and I highly recommend for anyone who takes hundreds of photos or videos and does not have enough space to save them all.

title: Couldn't get Along without Google Photos
content:
Couldn't get Along without Google Photos. I love having Google Photos app on my phone. I back up all my photos very often & delete all the photos from my phone. I like being able to then work with my photos on my laptop on Google Photos. The sync has worked instantly for me. I like that Google Photos organizes some of my photos into albums, and then I make other albums on my own, to share with family members. Great feature. 
Maybe I just haven't found the correct setting yet, but I would like it if Google Photos would just automatically take the photos from my phone whenever I am connected to wifi. So I give it 4 out of 5 stars, with the only issue being ease of use for a 50-something who tries hard to
Keep up on the technology.

title: Great app to organize your photos ( free)
content: Great app to organize your photos ( free). This a useful app! While they reduce the size of your pictures a bit, they are still good in quality for print for a free service. You can make albums, share them, and even collaborate with others to add pictures from different devices! Google makes it easier and easier to find events, places and people in an increasing mega library of digital pictures you can't possibly keep in your phone unless you back them up somewhere else that will be either inconvenient or will cost you some money on a subscription. There is room for improvement: a smoother switch from different accounts, where photos from profesional personal accounts don’t mix (right now, I find it impossible!)

title: I like it.
content: I like it.. I had google photos app for years and will always have it. I like that Its no hassle in putting my pictures into different albums.  The only issue was I bought a Google storage disk for my photos to clear up some of my space. I bought this particular one because it was recommended by Google for exactly to store pictures from Google photos. Didn’t work and it wasn’t cheap. So I guess that forces me to pay extra money for Google cloud for more space. My problem with that it’s not easy to get my pictures from the cloud when I want it. Overall I do like google photos but I have to use another app for photos as well for storage and may not have some other things google offers in it. But I can get to my old photos and videos when I want it much easier with the other.

title: Google Photos app makes me cry
content: Google Photos app makes me cry. I want to thank the developers of this app for the intuitive features that take photos based on face recognition to create surprise mini movies for me, complete with accompanying music.  I open the app to find these surprises on a regular basis and can’t help but be filled with happy tears for all the beautiful memories!  The stylized photos are also another great feature of the app.  My photos are available from any platform, whenever I need them, which is the best, and I’ve never encountered any app issues.    I’ve went from the surprise (many years ago) of finding David Hasselhoff inserted into photos, to the joy of a special Mother’s Day movie, a few weeks ago; don’t hesitate to make this your go-to photo app!  Thanks Google!❤️

title: Best free image tool I use
content:
Best free image tool I use. I honestly can say this is the best free image tool I use. I bought a Pixel 2 for many of its features, Google Photos was not one of them. I use this with my Pixel 2, Droid Turbo 2, iPad, iPod Touch and now my computer.

The ability to make animations, and the sharing are amazing, but what I truly love is the ability to tag people and pets. It is so easy to be sitting with a friend and simply click their face and be able to share all the photos I have with that person in them. I even use it when talking to my doctor because I copied many of my X-ray pictures and I can pull them up quicker then the doctors system just by searching for ‘ XRay ‘ even if I never tagged the image in any way. The search feature is simply magic.

Thank you! Thank you!

title: Needs some tweaks.
content:
Needs some tweaks.. I find Google photos app to be very good. I love the auto back up feature. I have mine set so that it will only back up my photos when my phone is on Wi-Fi to conserve my cellular data.

One feature that I find lacking is the ability to do some more complex photo manipulation tasks. Google photos does let you do basic photo manipulation cropping and such. They've been buying a lot of companies that have made photo processing applications. What I have read in the trade magazines is that they were going to incorporate these apps into Google photos. And that is not been done.  I am not asking for a complete  Photoshop app within Google Photos. However, it would certainly be nice to have something beyond the most basic of photo manipulation tasks with in the Google photos application instead of having to go in and out of various other apps.

title: Use this as a backup of your backup
content:
Use this as a backup of your backup. I have read a lot of reviews where people loose all of their photos. 
Here are my tips and suggestions to prevent that, 
{the app has 2 ways to delete}
*delete by the trash can* 
*delete by the “3 dot icon”* (I’m on iPhone)
Trash can deletes the photo EVERYWHERE, if the original photo is still on the device, it will delete it both. 
The icon allows you to “delete device original* (this is the safe and correct way if you are wanting to back up your photos) this way will only delete the photo that is on your phone - but it will keep a copy stored in google photos. 

I use google photos as a bridge on my phone to backup my photos until I have enough time to manually back them up to my external hard drive. 

I also have my settings on google photos set to backup while using cellular data - that way they are always getting backed up - not just when I’m hooked up to WiFi (which is the default of the app). I would select the cellular option if you have unlimited data. 

I love this app and I personally have not had any issues by following those steps. 
It is incredible to have a FREE cloud backup for photos!

title: THE BEST PHOTO APP
content: THE BEST PHOTO APP. I absolutely love Google Photos. It highlights different photos for me to look at and asks if I’d like to order prints. The prints are so affordable and delivered to me. This helps me to accomplish what I keep telling myself to do but keep procrastinating on. The app automatically downloads any photo I take on my phone and safely keeps it. It also suggests photos that can be safely deleted, either because they are screenshots or blurred photos. And Google Photos alerts me when my phone needs more space. It tells me the number of photos that have been safely backed up to Google’s cloud and asks if I’d like to delete these photos from my phone to free up space. Obviously I can’t say enough good things about this app.

title: The new AI search feature is garbage
content:
The new AI search feature is garbage. How the original Google photos search feature worked before they incorporated their terrible Gemini ai into the app was perfect. I could search for anything and find my photos with ease. 
Today I was getting a haircut, I'm trying to find a picture from the last time my hair was cut so I could provide my barber a reference, the Gemini ai after I simply searched "hair cut" gave me photos from my camera roll from five years ago at the top of the search, followed by any photo ever that has hair in it?! 
This was not an issue before, I used to he able to just search for haircut, scroll down a little bit and spot my reference photo with ease. 
The Gemini feature in the app is not new, it's been about half a year from what I remember, but they did remove the option to opt out of the ai and use the original search feature, however that is now missing, and the search functionality is useless.

title: amazing, truly incredible !!
content:
amazing, truly incredible !!. i've been struggling with my phone's storage for a long time now because i'm such a nostalgic person and i refuse to delete old photos and videos; believing that one day i'd like to look back and reminisce, or i keep them just in case i ever needed them again in the future.

of course, that resulted in lots and lots of storage being taken up by them, up to 60GB. my phone ran out of storage very soon, so i went to my friends to ask for help. one of them owns a google pixel phone and recommended i use google photos.

they convinced me it'd be worth it because the photos'll never disappear, as they're connected to my already existing gmail account. they also said once google photos is done backing up any photos/videos, it offers to delete them off your phone so that you don't have to go and do that yourself.

i trusted my friend with that and gave it a try, and i couldn't have been more grateful for google. thank you so so much for this app. it has freed so much space for me and i still have full access to my precious photos and videos <3

it's really worth more than 5 stars

title: Person & Pet Recognition
content:
Person & Pet Recognition. I enjoy Google Photos. Seamlessly works in the background and doesn’t always notify you of historical items. 2 suggestions that would move this to 5 stars. 1) ability to select a person to add to the person and pet recognition feature. It’s great at recognizing people and amazingly is able to discern the same person over the years from child / baby photos to adult photos. 

2) read the dates on scanned photos and suggest correcting the date the photo was taken. I have thousands of photos a family member scanned that are all marked on the same day. I can manually update them but that is going to take a while. It would be incredible (and a little creepy) if Google could suggest a rough timeframe based on what people are wearing and where they are in the aging process.

title: Works well, but needs improvement
content: Works well, but needs improvement. I love this app, but Google needs some improvements. You can search based on the NAME of the photo. I will name a photo so that if I need to find it, I can. Well, found out that it WON’T work. You can search by file name! Crazy. Duplicate photos are a huge issue. No way to deal with that on a sensible basis. Searching by address would be nice, since you have the location. Seems like you can only search by area, and that’s not specific enough to find needed results. I still miss a lot of features the old Picassa had, which google took over then shut down. Why remove all those great features? However searching by name or face works pretty amazingly. Searching by a description works better than expected. Overall I love this app, but please bring back old features and improve on existing ones. Listen to your clients!

title: Great app
content:
Great app. **Update*** 
App seems to take forever backing up videos these last few months. It takes so long I have just deleted the videos so it can back up my photos. 

Not only does this app back up quickly and efficiently it offers great tools to build a story from your pictures. After our trip to Miami was backed up. I was surprised over the course of two days with different projects the app had designed showcasing our trip. The different designs were fantastic and really brought to life our entire trip. With the last few updates it has become easier to build these projects myself, which I love. Oh yeah and it backs up even faster; which I didn't think was possible. And tie in the fact you can log in through the website and see all your pictures wherever you are.

title: Almost perfect.
content:
Almost perfect.. This app does feel a little limited on what you can do related to backing up photos and videos. I haven’t found any option to skip a photo/video you don’t want to back up unless you delete it. Another small problem is that when you back up all of your gallery to Google Photos the app itself will be the amount of GB all of your gallery is. And if you don’t delete it it’s the same thing as having your gallery duplicated. ALSO the auto back up feature is kind of broken when trying to back up couple hundred photos, it will stop even if you have background refresh turned on. I had to sleep with my phone unlocked doing the backup because I was unsure it would work with it turned off. Great app overall just has some small issues that bothers me.
-Iphone 6s

title: It's been the best for so long, it's getting hard to compete with itself
content:
It's been the best for so long, it's getting hard to compete with itself. Sadly I've grown bored with Google Photos. I wish it did more. 

Storage
Already being a Google One subscriber, it says there's nothing I can do to upgrade as I near capacity. Wish there was some kind of built-in review to capture inadvertent excess and prompt you with an action like download and delete or deep storage transfer to Drive or Dropbox. There's also no way to see where the top offenders for size are including large and/or long videos, exorbitantly large raw image formats, etc. 

Backend storage options
Honestly doesn't make sense that there wouldn't be a backend for storage hand-off. Still keeps people connected and using the software. Just allows easier transition to alternative storage. I would rather be holding my own roll of film.

Shared album limitations
I've also gotten feedback from friends about not being able to filter a shared album, if for example we share a single Google photos album and we all contribute, how do I see only the ones that I took exclusively, or ones for 2 but not there other 6.

Search
But of course I do admit that I love the object and people recognition searches. Beyond the storage, that's what I'm here for.

title: Google Account Storage Problems
content:
Google Account Storage Problems. READ THIS IF YOU HAVE STORAGE PROBLEMS!!!

I downloaded Google Photos and allowed access to all my photos. I could no longer use my Gmail due to a full storage. I was afraid that if I deleted the Google Photos app that my camera roll would delete. I ended up changing Google Photos permissions in settings to not allow access to my camera roll. Then I deleted the app. I went to the Google Photos webpage on my computer and deleted all of the photos stored there. After that my Google Account gained its storage back because I am able to send and receive emails, however I am still seeing a notification that my storage is full. When I look at my storage it says that it actually isn’t full. Regardless, my camera roll retained all of its photos and I can now send and receive emails. I believe that whole process was not designed or explained well. I could not find any help or suggestions from Google.
